stories.body:
The NBA is only a few games deep, but leaguewide buzz never stops.

The LeBron James and Jaylen Brown era with the Philadelphia 76ers got off to an ideal start by spoiling ring night for the New York Knicks. The Detroit Pistons also returned to their regular-season dominance with a win over the Boston Celtics, and the Oklahoma City Thunder struck the first rivalry blow against the San Antonio Spurs this season.

Now, what will Giannis Antetokounmpo's first season away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their impact this season?

All season, bookmark this page for the latest news and reactions from our ESPN NBA insiders.

Hoop Collective: Is Houston an NBA Finals sleeper? And 76ers' dream start

Brian is joined by ESPN's Tim MacMahon to discuss the Houston Rockets' 6-1 start and whether they are a legitimate title contender. They then break down why Kyrie Irving might not be traded this season if the Dallas Mavericks' continue their impressive start to the season. Next, they check in on the injured Oklahoma City Thunder, the hot Memphis Grizzlies and the dream start for LeBron James and the Philadelphia 76ers.

MacMahon on Kyrie's future in Dallas: "When I'm talking to executives and scouts around the league ... when the Mavericks come up, it is the No. 1 thing people are asking me about.

"You know, going into the season, I would have said more likely than not, [Irving] gets moved by the deadline, but I didn't feel super strong about it. The more I see the team, the more I'm around the team, the more I think it's going to be awfully hard to trade him.

"Not that there won't be a big market -- there will be, but if they've got a chance to compete for a play-in and playoff spot, I just think it's going to be really tough to move Kyrie. Also, just as much as he means to that locker room and as well as he's working with Cooper [Flagg], it was beautiful basketball.

"And just basketball wise they are a phenomenal fit. And I do think there's a legitimate argument to be made for the value of playing meaningful games in March and April for the development of a superstar like Cooper, of young role players like Zaccharie Risacher, who, by the way, is doing some really interesting things -- on the defensive end especially -- and he's got a player option next year.

"I think it's a situation where you can get together and handle it in the summer. It's not like you have to either move them or lose them, by this deadline."

How Dybantsa will impact the Wizards on the court

After missing the first four games of the season with an ankle injury, No. 1 pick AJ Dybantsa will make his regular-season debut Wednesday, ESPN's Shams Charania reported.

Dybantsa's arrival could give the Wizards one of the best starting lineups in the Eastern Conference -- which would be quite a change of pace for a team that hasn't won 20 games in a season since 2022-23. Anthony Davis has been explosive and productive through four games. Trae Young is averaging 22 points and a league-best 11 assists per game. And Kyshawn George is up to 18 PPG as he continues to make strides as an all-around NBA contributor. Add Dybantsa to that mix and there's legitimate reason for excitement in Washington.

The only downside is that Dybantsa should command plenty of playing time, which could further squeeze an overcrowded Wizards rotation. Already, 2025 first-rounder Will Riley has seen his playing time crater, but he, Tre Johnson and Bilal Coulibaly are all wings who will now likely come off the bench, yet deserve the opportunity to continue their development. -- Zach Kram

What are the Warriors' options on Porzingis?

ESPN's Anthony Slater detailed the Golden State Warriors' options regarding center Kristaps Porzingis and his lingering health issues in a report today.

[Stephen] Curry twice made sure to mention the human component, expressing sympathy for Porzingis, who has made public the lingering impact he said he still feels after contracting an upper respiratory viral illness while with the Boston Celtics two seasons ago.

"We always said availability was a big factor for our team with all the guys we have out," Curry said. "It's no secret that the [center] spot is an important one for us, especially with his skill set. It's hard to talk about without keeping the humanity of it in mind. But it is a tough one to figure out."

Team sources continue to express an extreme level of pessimism that Porzingis will ever play for the Warriors again, but he could end up helping the organization in another way, because his contract, which is only guaranteed for $3 million next season, could still prove to be valuable in executing a trade.

Marks on the Thunder's next steps following crucial injuries: "I think the long term, Brian and Tim, is that you will apply for this disabled player exception for Jalen Williams. I don't think you'll get it for Cason Wallace because you have to be deemed out until June 15. And I don't think that Wallace injury will get you there. I think the Jalen Williams injury will. But that doesn't eliminate him coming back. Just because you apply for it doesn't eliminate the player actually returning. That exception will be worth $15 million. You can only sign or trade for a player in the last year of their contract.

"Their biggest trade assets are those trade exceptions that were created in the Lu Dort, Aaron Wiggins, and Isaiah Joe trades that range from $17 to, I don't know, $8 million. And you can trade for players on multi-year deals. Now, threshold on this is probably $7 million, right? You're $6.9 below that second apron. I don't think there's an appetite to go in there, but I think there is an appetite to spend because they went out and did that offer sheet on Spencer Jones. That would have added to their payroll another $23 million-$24 million.

"So I think that's kind of what you're looking at. You're evaluating guys in that $7-million-to-below range from a roster standpoint, but I also think you can even go north of that if let's say [Nikola] Topic is not going to be a factor this year and he needs to be part of a deal down the road. But that's the long-term picture ... You're basically just trying to hold on right now and then basically figure it out when you get to December."

What Edwards' injury means for Wolves

On Monday, Anthony Edwards looked like an MVP candidate as he poured in 47 points in Cleveland. On Tuesday, that dream was dashed early, as ESPN's Shams Charania reported that Edwards will miss up to two months due to right knee surgery.

Minnesota can still contend this season, as long as Edwards returns healthy at the end of that projected time frame. The partnership of Edwards and LaMelo Ball was one of the most exciting elements of the new season, and the Timberwolves raced to a 3-1 start featuring three blowout wins, with an overtime loss to the Cavaliers marring their ledger. At the end of two more months, 52 games will remain on their schedule.

But they won't be comfortable in the meantime. The Timberwolves have a relatively shallow roster, and their bench will be stretched thin once sixth man Ayo Dosunmu moves into the starting lineup to replace Edwards. Their two-way star's absence also reduces any margin for error with the rest of the roster; Ball is notoriously injury-prone, and if both guards are ever out at the same time, a lengthy losing streak could ensue.

Edwards to undergo surgery, miss up to two months

Minnesota Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards will undergo an arthroscopic procedure on his ailing right knee that will sideline him for up to two months, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.

"But it seemed clear right before camp that he was fading away from basketball, obviously dealing with this health issue and thinking about his future. He calls Mike Dunleavy the day before training camp, basically tells him he's not coming in to work, he's going to go deal with this health thing.

"He showed up for one meeting two weeks into camp as the Warriors team was in Las Vegas. He met with Mike Dunleavy and Rick Celebrini. Then he left the facility and hasn't returned and has not been around the team to the point that when we put out the report yesterday, the Warriors didn't address some of the trade speculation, but did say he will not be around the team in the immediate future.

Marks: Warriors have hurdles in a potential Porzingis deal
Following the news that the Warriors are exploring deals, finding a trade early in the season for Kristaps Porzingis could be difficult.

First, Golden State is hard capped at the second apron and isn't allowed to take back more salary than what is sent out. The Warriors are allowed to aggregate salaries if they are receiving less money in return.

Second, since teams are in the evaluation periods of their rosters, trades are uncommon early in the season.

Under the current CBA, there have only been two regular season trades in the months of October and November. -- Bobby Marks

Ishbia on the future of NBA expansion: "Well, I'm supportive of growing the game. So I'm pro expansion.

"Obviously, it depends on the situation and making sure that it's the right partners because they're now partners with us. And the right value, but also are they doing the right things for the fans? I believe that Vegas is a market that we need to fill. I think Seattle's one. I know there's been talk about Mexico City. The way I look at it is expanding the game. The NBA is a global game. And so having 30 is a limited number. Can you get to 32? I mean, can you go that many more? So, it's like, can you grow? Can you cover a big market like Vegas?

"I don't care that it's close to Phoenix. I'm excited. I think there's abundance. There's opportunity everywhere. And I'm supportive of it."

Ishbia on the outlook of the 2026-27 NBA season: "First off, there's a lot more balance. The East definitely got stronger. The West is extremely strong. But let's put it aside.

"There's also no tanking. So there's not five free wins, eight free wins. And in the East last year, a lot of teams really compounded that because there was about seven teams, six teams trying to lose, which is horrible for our game. NBA Adam Silver did a great job. We got rid of that. So there's no tanking.

"People are going to win -- 45 wins is a hell of a season. And I think it's going to be very, very tough. And I think that might be a 4, 5, 6 seed where last year it was 50, 52 wins to get to that level. And so, I think that's not been talked about enough."

Marks: A busy weekend of transaction expected
The last weekend of the offseason is expected to bring a flurry of transactions.

Starting on Saturday Oct. 17, teams will need to decide on players signed to non-guaranteed contracts. If a player is on the roster past 5 p.m. ET, teams will begin incurring a per day salary charge.

For example, the New York Knicks would be charged $17,622 per day against the cap if James Wiseman is not waived by Saturday. However, despite a mandate to remain under the second apron, New York is allowed to keep Wiseman and Bruce Brown to start the season.

The deadline for rookie extensions is Monday by 6 p.m. ET.

Since the start of the offseason, five players -- Victor Wembanyama, Amen and Ausar Thompson, Keyonte George and Brandin Podziemski -- have signed rookie extensions. The 2023 rookie class of extended players are below the per year average of 11 players we have seen since 2023.

Some of the notable names to watch include Brandon Miller and Cason Wallace. Keep in mind that out of the 34 players who signed rookie extensions in the prior three seasons, 17 came on the last day of eligibility.

The rookie extension deadline is not the only date teams are paying attention to, however. Oct. 19 is also the deadline to extend veterans who have two years left on their contract -- not including an option year -- and the last day to reduce rosters to 15 players on standard contracts. -- Bobby Marks

Detroit Pistons coach J.B. Bickerstaff has held many offseason conversations with All-NBA guard Cade Cunningham about seizing greatness and the necessary steps toward improving after last year's playoff run that stretched to Game 7 of the Eastern Conference semifinals.

Bickerstaff has guaranteed "a better version" Cunningham this season, which could be a scary sight after he averaged 23.9 points, 9.9 assists, 5.5 rebounds and 1.4 steals in 33.9 minutes during 2025-26. But Cunningham also led the East in turnovers per game after finishing with the second most in 2024-25.

"I don't have to challenge Cade, and that's why he is who he is," Bickerstaff said. "Because he's pulling. He's not being pushed."

Cunningham showed up in a fresh pair of Nike S.T. Charge "Detroit Tough" sneakers in Pistons colors. He will also receive his own signature Nike shoe, which is expected to debut during the second half of the season.

"I'm thankful to be in these shoes. I'm thankful to have the opportunity to represent my family in this way," Cunningham said. "Represent where I come from, but then to represent the city of Detroit.

"In a city like this, it's a blessing. I'm thankful for it, I don't take it for granted and I'm trying to make the most out of it." -- Eric Woodyard

Hornets waive former No. 8 pick Dillingham

The Charlotte Hornets are waiving guard Rob Dillingham, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Dillingham was traded from the Chicago Bulls on Saturday for Buddy Hield and cash. The Hornets created a $9.6 million trade exception with the move.

Dillingham, 21, appeared in 30 games for the Bulls last season, averaging 9.6 points and 2.8 assists.

SGA on chance at historic third straight MVP

At Oklahoma City Thunder media day, guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander discussed the possibility of winning a third straight NBA MVP award and whether that's something he ponders going into this season.

"No different than any other year: Try to be the best player I can be, try to implement the things I just worked on," Gilgeous-Alexander said.

"The decision for MVP is literally 82 games away. I'm not going to win the award in the first week of the season. ... That kind of recipe for me in the past has kind of worked, and I've been fortunate to win two in a row.

"We need to be laser focused on ourselves. We need to take the lessons from that [Western Conference finals] series, for sure, and we did. But it's certainly not something that we overcorrect for, because you end up chasing your shadow, and it prevents you from being your best as you move forward."

ESPN's Summer Forecast gave Gilgeous-Alexander the fourth-best chance at the 2027 MVP, behind Victor Wembanyama, Nikola Jokic and Luka Doncic. No player has won three consecutive MVPs since Larry Bird in 1984, 1985 and 1986. -- Baxter Holmes

Doncic talks LeBron exit, Lakers "championship" ceiling
Speaking to ESPN's Brian Windhorst during Los Angeles Lakers media day, guard Luka Doncic detailed his reaction to LeBron James leaving for the Philadelphia 76ers this past summer and why he thinks a successful 2026-27 includes a Lakers run to the title:

"It was kind of sad. Playing with LeBron was amazing. There's a lot of things I learned from him. ... We all know who LeBron James is."

Shams: Duren's relationship with Pistons "has fractures"

Simmons "didn't touch a ball for a year"

During Sacramento Kings media day, guard Ben Simmons laid out the reasons he chose the Kings and why he's excited for the 2026-27 season.

"The expectations are low. I feel like that's been something on me too, so we can relate in that way," Simmons told reporters. "I think we have a chip on our shoulder."

Simmons last played in 2024-25, appearing in 51 games for the Brooklyn Nets and LA Clippers. The three-time All-Star said the time away gave him the chance to focus on "getting my body right and my mind right."

Pistons GM hasn't spoken with Duren all summer

Jalen Duren and the Detroit Pistons have a decision to make as the clock ticks closer to Oct. 1 -- the deadline to sign a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer.

For Duren, he can accept the five-year, $200 million contract that has been offered by Detroit or he can become the first player named All-NBA or All-Star to sign the qualifying offer. If he chooses the latter, Duren will hold veto power on any trade this season and be an unrestricted free agent next summer.

For the Pistons, weighing the risk of having an All-NBA player on a one-year contract and, more importantly, the likelihood he will depart next summer as a free agent is key.

There are eight projected teams that have significant cap space to sign Duren to a four-year, $189 million max contract.

"I can't control the different things that he does or his group does," Pistons president of basketball operations Trajan Langdon said at media day. "For me, it's control what we can and letting him know he is a big part of what we do."

Langdon also said he hasn't spoken with Duren all summer during Pistons media day. -- Bobby Marks

Mitchell: LeBron to Cavs made sense "for a lot of reasons"

At Cavaliers media day, Donovan Mitchell said that in his mind, he thought LeBron James would return to Cleveland because "for a lot of reasons it made sense."

"I didn't think Philly. I thought if he didn't come here, it'd be Golden State," Mitchell said.

After being swept in the Eastern Conference finals by the eventual champion New York Knicks then missing out on James in free agency, Cleveland kept its core intact. The Cavs signed Mitchell to a four-year, $273 million maximum extension and re-signed James Harden to a three-year, $97 million contract. Cleveland did make one major addition by acquiring Peyton Watson from the Denver Nuggets in a multiteam trade then signing the restricted free agent to a four-year, $88 million deal.

Speaking for the first time since their extensions, Mitchell and Harden both said their approaches to their new deals -- Mitchell signing as soon as he was eligible with Harden opting out to give Cleveland more flexibility to make moves -- reflected a team-first mindset.

"This is something that I want to do, and I want to win a championship," Harden said. "So, what does that look like? Making the team better, making the team whole to where we give ourselves a chance. By the way, you can have the best talented team, which I've been on before, and still not win.

"We waited, waited, waited until the front office called me, made sure that we got everything that we can get, and then we signed. We got a long way to go, but I love the direction and steps that we're taking here as a unit from top to bottom." -- Daniel Oyefusi

MacMahon: Thunder adjusting to roster changes
The departures of three championship-winning teammates doesn't yet feel like reality for Thunder superstar Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, who kidded that he still expected Luguentz Dort, Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins to show up for Oklahoma City's team picture Monday afternoon.

"It's the business of the NBA, right?" Gilgeous-Alexander said, referring to the series of financially motivated trades. "I don't think anybody has played with all 12 guys their whole career. It sucks a little bit.

"My mind never even went to what we were going to be like on the court. It was more like the brotherhood."

As fellow OKC guard Jalen Williams added, "It's the weirdest thing ever." -- Tim MacMahon

Clippers announce Ingram has partially torn Achilles

The LA Clippers announced they found a partially torn Achilles tendon in Brandon Ingram's foot after his recent heel surgery. He will miss the start of the 2026-27 season.

Jokic: "I'm gonna sign next year"

Denver Nuggets center Nikola Jokic reiterated his commitment to the franchise at Monday's media day.

"I'm gonna sign next year," Jokic said. "If they want me."

Curry said knee is ready to go for the season

Golden State Warriors superstar guard Stephen Curry addressed the media Monday in offering positive updates on his injured knee.

"Knee's feeling great. Ready to go. No issues," Curry said. "I feel a lot stronger and understanding of what I'm dealing with."

Curry did acknowledge a "management element" but said there are currently no restrictions.

Nuggets confident in Jokic's future with franchise

Members of the Denver Nuggets' front office, general manager Jon Wallace and executive vice president of basketball Ben Tenzer addressed the media on Monday and answered questions regarding Nikola Jokic's future with the franchise. The three-time MVP didn't sign an extension this offseason.

"We feel very comfortable with the relation and trust there," Tenzer said. "We have no concerns."

LeBron: I wanted to finish my career with the Knicks
New Philadelphia 76er LeBron James said his decision came down to five teams this offseason and that he envisioned going to the New York Knicks before they won the 2026 title.

"I had visions of playing in [Madison Square] Garden and finishing my career in the Garden," James told ESPN on Monday during the 76ers' media day. "One of the best places I've ever played.

"I think it's the No. 1 arena in the world, as far as for a basketball player. But after they beat San Antonio, I was like, 'Hey, I can't.' I couldn't do it."

James and the 76ers will play the Knicks at the Garden on opening night, Oct. 20.

No update on Gary Trent Jr. investigation

Milwaukee Bucks governor Wes Edens did not provide an update on the league investigation into Gary Trent Jr.'s contract.

"I don't have any update," Edens said. "We're working with the league and fully cooperating with them. But I don't have any insight beyond that."

The NBA is looking into a potential cap-circumvention violation by the Bucks around Trent's deal this offseason.

Cronin: Blazers have "belief" in Ja Morant
Portland Trail Blazers' general manager Joe Cronin addressed why the franchise decided to trade for Ja Morant this offseason during Portland's media day on Monday.

"Just straight belief in Ja," Cronin said. "Our view of Ja as still a very high-level player.

"I'm sure there will be questions about fit, but we're very focused on talent."

Cronin also said veteran guard Jrue Holiday could play some minutes on the wing for Portland this season, while adding that Holiday and veteran guard Damian Lillard will have a positive influence on Morant.

Kerr: Rookie Lendeborg going to "play a ton"

Golden State Warriors coach Steve Kerr said during Monday's media day that he expects rookie Yaxel Lendeborg to "play a ton" this season.

"He's clearly going to play a ton," Kerr said. "He gives us the size and the versatility that we need.

"Whether he's a starter or coming off the bench, that will be determined the next couple of weeks."

Lendeborg was the No. 11 pick in the 2026 NBA draft and averaged 15.1 points per game at Michigan last season.

Embiid: 'Extremely excited' about this year's team
Philadelphia 76ers center Joel Embiid said Monday that he feels like the team finally has the right mix of players, after an offseason in which the franchise traded for Jaylen Brown and signed LeBron James to join the young guard tandem of VJ Edgecombe and Tyrese Maxey.

"It's hard to win when you get a group of guys together for one year, two years, maybe," he said. "I'm extremely excited about this team because we have the right mix of veteran leadership and younger guys. We might have some ups and downs, but we're gonna get there."

Wembanyama addresses last year's Finals loss
After leading by double digits in each of the five games in last season's NBA Finals, San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama said his memories of it will fuel the team this season.

"I couldn't imagine a better motivation," he said.

Harper addresses role for coming season
After offseason chatter about his role, San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper said he'd follow the coaches' lead this season.

"Everyone has a competitive edge to them. But the biggest thing for me is whatever I can do, just like last year, to help the team win," he said. "Whatever position the coaches think is best for me to be in, that's the position I'll happily go in."

First look at LeBron in a 76ers uniform
New Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James is taking questions from reporters on Monday. Here's what he had to say when asked about his initial impressions of his team:

"Everybody is on the same page," James said. "We are all speaking the same language."

LeBron addressed his role too, saying he's open to whatever the team needs from him to win.

"Whatever they need me to do," he said. "The luxury of my game is I can do everything. ... Literally, I can do everything"

Kawhi: I was a distraction, ready to move forward
In his first public appearance with the Toronto Raptors after a controversy-filled summer, Kawhi Leonard addressed the NBA's investigation into him and his business dealings.

"I know why some of you guys came. You want to hear about the investigation. But in talking with the NBA and PA, I think the best decision is to move forward and focus on my time being a Toronto Raptor," he said. "I already was a distraction for the past 70 days and wasn't able to meet my teammates or do any of that stuff, minicamp stuff, so, moving forward, I just want to talk about the Toronto Raptors."

Haliburton: I am 100% healthy
Indiana Pacers guard Tyrese Haliburton said Monday that he is healthy and ready for the season.

"I am healthy. I am 100%," he said. "There will be no restrictions. That is not news. There is no source. I am the source. I am ready to go for the year."

Porzingis out indefinitely in blow to Warriors
Golden State Warriors big man Kristaps Porzingis is out indefinitely to open training camp with a health issue, according to the team.
In late July, Porzingis agreed to a two-year, $40 million contract with a player option on the second season to return to the Warriors.

Brown: KAT, Hart extension talks won't be a distraction
After reports surfaced last week that negotiations between the New York Knicks and center Karl-Anthony Towns had hit a stalemate, coach Mike Brown said Monday neither Towns' situation nor Hart's would linger in the locker room.

"We talk about everything [with the team]," Brown said. "We don't want to have any elephants in the room."

"I'm not involved in it. They'll figure it out. Control what you can control."

And here's what Towns said about a potential extension: "I've made it known I want to play here. Been a fan since I was a kid. I'd like to get it done."

Hornets GM: Brandon Miller to be ready for training camp
After undergoing offseason surgery on his left shoulder, Hornets wing Brandon Miller should be a full participant in training camp and "ready to roll" for opening night, Hornets general manager Jeff Peterson said Monday.

Miller, 23, is entering his fourth NBA season after being the No. 2 pick in the 2023 draft.

Duren won't be at Pistons media day, start of camp
Detroit Pistons All-Star center Jalen Duren is not attending the team's media day on Monday or the start of training camp as his contract standoff continues, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Monday.

Duren, a restricted free agent, is declining the team's five-year, $200 million fully guaranteed offer as both sides remain at a stalemate ahead of the Thursday deadline on a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer, sources said.

Sept. 26

Bulls trade Dillingham to Hornets for Hield, cash
The Chicago Bulls and Charlotte Hornets agreed to a trade sending Rob Dillingham to Charlotte for Buddy Hield and cash, the teams announced Saturday.

2026 NBA offseason trade grades

Sept. 25

What's next for Curry and the Warriors?
Stephen Curry's two-year, $116 million extension made him the first player in NBA history to amass $600 million in career on-court earnings.

The deal has also put the Golden State Warriors in position to have extra spending power next summer.

By Curry taking $10 million less than the maximum allowed, the Warriors project to have nearly $38 million in cap space in 2027. Golden State could increase its projection to $55 million if center Kristaps Porzingis is waived in the offseason. Porzingis' $20 million salary for next season is guaranteed for $3 million.

For Golden State to have ample room, forwards Draymond Green and Jimmy Butler III would need to sign elsewhere or at a significantly lesser salary. They will be free agents next summer.

Both salary projections include the $17 million free agent hold of guard Brandin Podziemski. The 2023 first-round pick is eligible until Oct. 19 to extend his contract. -- Bobby Marks

Grading the Curry deal: Why Warriors don't get an A

Hornets star Knueppel sidelined by hamstring injury
The Charlotte Hornets announced that Kon Knueppel will be out for at least the entire preseason because of a left hamstring injury.

James: Maxey, Embiid were factors in joining 76ers
LeBron James said his longstanding friendship with All-Star Tyrese Maxey and a desire to help Joel Embiid win his first NBA title played significant roles in his decision to sign a two-year, $8 million contract with the Philadelphia 76ers in July.

"[Embiid has] done everything in our league, and the only thing he has not done is win a championship. And I want to try to help him get that first one," James said. "He has a city on his back. He's been 'The Process' for 10 years, 12 years, however long he's been there. But I think it's time we even get you deeper into the process. And I hope that I can be, kind of, that final little piece that can help him get over the hump."

Grizzlies waive Russell
The Memphis Grizzlies have waived D'Angelo Russell, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Russell has made one All-Star team during his career and was selected No. 2 in the 2015 NBA draft.

stories.headline: Who's No. 1? Our definitive ranking of the NHL's new Hometown Remix jerseys
stories.summary: Here is our ranking of the 32 NHL Hometown Remix jerseys for the 2026-27 season.
stories.body:
The NHL Hometown Remix jerseys are here, and some of them are spectacular.

And some of them aren't.

When Fanatics became the NHL's official on-ice uniform outfitter in the 2024-25 season, it was expected to take a couple of seasons before attempting its first "all 32 teams" alternate jersey project, like the Reverse Retro jerseys Adidas created for the NHL in 2020 and 2022.

"It was always envisioned with 'How do we do something different than what Adidas did with Reverse Retro 1.0 and 2.0?'" said Brian Jennings, NHL chief branding officer and senior executive vice president.

Enter NHL Hometown Remix jerseys, which officially launched Monday morning after weeks of tantalizing leaks.

The concept was simple: Have teams create distinct new looks that would theoretically tie back to the places they play and the fans for whom they play.

"When Hometown Remix came in and we started those conversations, I was like, 'OK, there's something here in this hyperlocal thing.' The part that got me really excited was the buy-in from the clubs," Jennings said.

Some teams seemed to really understand the assignment, and others sort of faked their way through it.

Here is our ranking of the 32 NHL Hometown Remix jerseys for the 2026-27 season, which (for now) is expected to be the only season in which they're worn.

We've reviewed the jerseys in person at Fanatics and have seen what they look like with a full uniform and on the ice. Our ranking is based on how good they look, how innovative they are and how well they tie in with the mission of the Hometown Remix jerseys.

Let's start with what we consider to be the best.

No. 1: Pittsburgh Penguins

Andy Warhol, then Andrew Warhola Jr., was born in Pittsburgh in 1928, nearly 40 years before the Penguins entered the NHL. His ties to the city -- home to The Andy Warhol Museum -- are part of a larger connection between the pop art movement and Pittsburgh, carried on by locals such as Burton Morris.

If the primary ethos of the Hometown Remix project is to connect the jersey to the city, then Pittsburgh gets enormous credit for doing it without relying on, say, architecture or weather phenomena. It doesn't mine franchise history for an obscure look from which to draw; it's reimagining the team's primary logo for the better part of 55 years, although it nods to previous team color schemes, too.

But that's only half the mission for the Hometown Remix jersey project. The other is "does this look good?"

We'd argue it looks the best.

Lost in the Microsoft Paint leak mockups was the offset outline around the Penguin, giving it a sense of motion while also being slightly disorienting. The dotted yellow background of the logo is like if Roy Lichtenstein were commissioned to create a Stadium Series jersey. It's the epitome of pop art: Something familiar, from the Igloo tribute on the shoulder to the numbers on the back, reinterpreted in a way that uses that nostalgia to push in a bold new direction.

There are probably very good, potentially litigious reasons they couldn't go full Warhol here -- imagine a jersey with the same four logos on the front done in the style of Warhol's Campbell's soup can? However, we did love the nod to his art on the hem as the word "Pittsburgh" is repeated several times in several colors to represent the city's different boroughs.

Both jersey rankings and art are inherently subjective. From our perspective, nothing in this batch of new sweaters married concept and execution better than the Penguins did. These are the best.

No. 2: Anaheim Ducks

Finally answering the question: What if Anaheim had entered the NHL leaning all the way in to its namesake and dressed like Gordon Bombay's Mighty Ducks?

Fanatics has a bunch of stuff in its media materials about the fresh green parks and golden sunsets of Orange County. But this is Charlie Conway. This is Marguerite Moreau. This is the Flying V and "fly together." This is "The Mighty Ducks," through and through. It's a jersey that would have 100% turned up in a SoCal hip-hop video voted No. 1 on "TRL" in 1998.

It also made us wonder whether New Orleans should get an NHL expansion team, because this jersey also looks a few shades (and bead necklaces) away from being Mardi Gras-ready.

No. 3: Florida Panthers

The Panthers had the best Reverse Retro 2.0 jersey back in 2022 when they finally made their stick-and-palm secondary logo their primary crest, ending a 30-year run of sweaters that did everything but evoke South Florida.

Well, there's no mistaking South Florida this time, folks! The Panthers run back that awesome logo augmented by a sunrise -- the team plays in Sunrise, for locality's sake -- whose colors are used throughout the jersey. That includes the most distinct and bold primary color ever seen on an NHL jersey.

They call it "coral." Everyone else will call it pink. Whatever you call it, the Panthers took a swing few have taken in a pro sports jersey -- although it should be noted that the MLS' Inter Miami walked so Florida could skate in "coral."

An undeniable facet of this jersey's success is that the right group of players is wearing them. Few teams are as in-your-face as the Panthers, literally and figuratively. The juxtaposition between some of the NHL's most unrelentingly nasty and physical players and a jersey that looks like a beach cocktail is intoxicating. Radko Gudas is going to throw one of these jerseys, folks. Let that soak in.

No. 4: Nashville Predators

Outside of some guitar strings on the numbers and piano keys in the collar, the Predators have never really leaned in to the honky-tonk of it all in Nashville. Creating a jersey that looks like country music stage wear -- from the flourishes on the shoulders to the filigree in the crest -- is such an obvious winner in retrospect. It's sort of amazing it took this long.

While many of us will be enthralled by a team that looks ready to play a cover of "I Walk the Line" at Tootsies, Predators fans are no doubt happy to see the team return to a sharp navy base for the first time in around 15 years. It's a valentine to the Broadway music bars near the arena, a nod to some great Predators uniforms of the past and just a stellar hockey jersey.

No. 5: Montreal Canadiens

It's hard to pull off an innovative and compelling white jersey, as evidenced by the Hometown Remix program having produced only four of them. The Canadiens' sweater is easily the best of that bunch and a contender for best overall, given how it looks and the story it tells.

On the sleeves: white pine, fleur-de-lys, rose, thistle and clover. The five symbols on the flag of Montreal, whose red and white colorway inform the rest of this design. The side panels are meant to evoke the eponymous Mount Royal. The number system is inspired by Old Montreal. The crest has texturing designed to honor the stonework around the city.

Montreal's specialty jerseys have typically dipped back into the franchise's history for inspiration -- remember the "barber pole" sweaters from its centennial celebration? Well, these keep the general template of a Canadiens jersey. There's a real audacity to the design, given the jerseys that have come before them. These sweaters are going to look magnifique on the ice and are a deeply detailed love letter to the city that loves its Habs endlessly.

No. 6: Washington Capitals

Amanda Tischler, the Capitals' senior vice president of marketing, told ESPN it was a happy accident that their Hometown Remix jersey runs back the Capitol dome logo the team wore when Alex Ovechkin entered the NHL, just as the Great 8 is in his final season in the league.

There are few other Hometown Remix jerseys that seem like they should have been a team's primary jersey sometime in the past. We're so accustomed to "Rock the Red" that we forget their jerseys didn't even have that color for about a dozen years in the 1990s and early aughts.

Along with the dome, the other local connection is the marble texturing of the sleeves and shoulder yoke. We think it's pretty innovative, but it's also understandable that some might see it as one gimmick too many. One person's "Wow, it looks like a D.C. monument!" is another person's "Why do the shoulders look dirty?"

No. 7: Detroit Red Wings

As you'll see later in this ranking, challenging an Original Six team to remix a nearly century-old look isn't easy. That especially goes for the Red Wings, whose Winged Wheel is one of the most iconic looks in sports. They're not going to suddenly bust out a purple jersey with an octopus maw on the front. They're just not.

The cephalopod is referenced on the hem of the jersey, but the rest of the sweater is dedicated to two dogmas: that the Red Wings' jerseys can't be improved on and that even in these dark times for the franchise, Detroit is still "Hockeytown." They've had words atop their logo before (such as on their 2014 Winter Classic sweaters) but had never had "Hockeytown" so front and center. These rock.

No. 8: Toronto Maple Leafs

There are a few jerseys in this ranking that could have finished much higher were it not for one or two missteps in design.

The good for Toronto: The remixing of its primary logo, with its eye-catching silhouette and intricate texturing that's carried over to the sleeves and the numbers. We also love that the various "Leafs" that have appeared on their jerseys are represented on the hem. The wordmark is large, making the whole front of the jersey a bit grandiose in keeping with the Centre of the Hockey Universe™.

The not as good for Toronto: Those white stripes harsh the vibe, don't they? Obviously, white sleeve striping on Leafs sweaters tracks back to 1927. But here, they just don't seem like a piece with the rest of the fit. They throw the whole thing off balance, like a confused spouse throwing multicolored carnations into a bouquet of a dozen roses.

No. 9: Carolina Hurricanes

Hot take: The Hurricanes need a new logo. This is a hard argument to make when they just lifted the Stanley Cup while wearing their swirly toilet flush logo, but the sentiment remains.

Whether this collegiate rendering of their mascot, Stormy, could ever become their primary mark is debatable, but it's a step up. The problem here is that the logo is featured on a drab gray sweater that's inferior to the team's red and black looks.

One thing we do like here: All the nods to the "City of Oaks," including oak leaves debossed on the sleeves.

No. 10: Vegas Golden Knights

Gambling references? On the uniform of a team based in Las Vegas? Is that even allowed?!

The Golden Knights finally lean in to casino iconography with felt table green on the shoulders, a roulette wheel pattern on the sleeves and socks, a typeface inspired by playing cards, and different card suits found around the jersey. Plus, there's an embossed script "Vegas" on the arms. It's a distinct look for the Knights that finally connects with everything around them on The Strip -- although it would have been fun to see the primary logo rendered in a winning slot machine combo. Maybe next time.

No. 11: Minnesota Wild

We went back and forth on this one. Black jerseys are beyond cliché. The Wild have traded in one of the NHL's most distinct color schemes for something that screams "recently relocated AHL franchise."

But this jersey improves mightily upon further inspection. Their primary logo has never looked better. The sleeves have a debossed Ursa Major and Ursa Minor, and the numbers have stars to evoke the Twin Cities. As an ode to cold Minnesota nights on the pond -- and the mysteries of space -- we're here for it.

No. 12: Dallas Stars

This is essentially a neon electrified version of the Stars' current road jerseys, with much bolder striping. The texture on the crest is supposed to be inspired by the city's skyline at night. Dallas could have gone a hundred ways with these jerseys, but the path it chose produced a stark on-ice look, if not exactly an innovative or city-specific one. But a must-own for fans of Monster Energy drink, one assumes.

No. 13: Columbus Blue Jackets

These would have gone so much harder had the Blue Jackets not worn their cannon as the primary crest of their 2025 NHL Stadium Series jerseys. These are still solid, and it's the first time the Blue Jackets have used gray as the base color for one of their jerseys. Maybe the best thing about these are the large stripes on the sleeves. The arching on them is in reference to Columbus being the "Arch City." They also threw a little "5th Line" graphic on the hem for the fans.

No. 14: Los Angeles Kings

The Kings are fighting history in their Hometown Remix look, which takes all their previous looks and puts them in a blender set to "streetwear."

The Kings did similar things to better success in their Reverse Retro 1.0 and 2.0 sweaters. These are still really solid and have some nice innovations -- the "Hollywood-inspired serif font" used for Los Angeles in the logo is sublime. But the palm leaves embossed on the sleeves are giving barbed-wire bicep tattoo from the 1990s.

No. 15: Tampa Bay Lightning

When the Tampa Bay Lightning released their Stadium Series jerseys last season, the hockey world had one question: "Hey, why wasn't that awesome Gasparilla-adjacent pirate skull logo on the shoulder the primary logo instead?" Maybe because it was already on deck for the Hometown Remix.

The David Bowie-esque lightning bolt on the skull -- and the missing tooth they gave it in this incarnation -- makes this one of the better alternate logos in hockey. But again, what could have been: Imagine how sweet these jerseys would be with a blue base and a black logo, rather than becoming the sixth variation of a black-based jersey in team history. (Don't they know black absorbs more heat and they play in Florida?)

No. 16: Seattle Kraken

Speaking of secondary logos that maybe deserve more prominence, the Kraken take their "Space Needle-as-anchor" logo from the shoulder to the front of the sweater, and it looks iconic. There are a lot of other local details on these, from a nod to Mt. Rainier on the sleeves to rhododendrons on the hem.

As Fanatics notes: "The new name and number system features custom nautical-inspired typography with meticulous scrimshaw embroidery, while the shoulder patch also brings scrimshaw detailing to the fore." One can never have enough scrimshaw.

No. 17: New York Islanders

The circle is complete. The fisherman jersey was one of the most widely mocked in NHL history, from the Islanders being called the "fish sticks" to those who felt its color scheme was reminiscent of toothpaste stripes. After being resurrected for Reverse Retro 2.0, the fisherman is back with something closer to the original colorway from the 1990s. The logo has never looked better, and the entire jersey system looks great on the ice. Consider yourself redeemed, Mr. Fishsticks.

No. 18: Ottawa Senators

This feels like a Pokémon evolution of their current jersey, like Ottawa got to a certain experience level and everything became "metallic gold lurex." The bilingual shoulder patches are a nice touch. The geometric striping on the sleeves is giving both Ottawa gothic architecture and Doctor Doom spellcasting runes.

No. 19: San Jose Sharks

The teeth. It's all about the teeth. The look is clean. The logo has a youthful vibe to it that fits the surging rebuild in San Jose, led by star Macklin Celebrini. But we can't get past the teeth on the sleeves, which is giving a video game-like "create-a-jersey" rather than an ascendant Stanley Cup contender.

OK, if we're being honest: It's not the teeth, it's the gums. So many gums. There's a reason one of the greatest summer blockbusters of all time wasn't called "Gums." Less gums, more jaws, please.

No. 20: Edmonton Oilers

Having a jersey that looks like it was dipped into a barrel of crude oil is either the greatest evocation of the Edmontonian aesthetic or a flimsy excuse to join the black jersey parade. Frankly, we were going to rank these a bit lower, but then someone mentioned they're reminiscent of the all-time classic World Cup of Hockey Team North America jerseys from 2016, which Connor McDavid also wore.

No. 21: Buffalo Sabres

We can already hear people grabbing their pitchforks over this mashup of iconic Buffalo Sabres looks being ranked so low. But just like how a DJ can cut together two classic songs to make a mediocre one, the Sabres' gorgeous blue sweaters mixed with "goat head" crests aren't in harmony.

This is the same issue we had back in 2022 when the Sabres put the "goat head" on a white-and-blue jersey for Reverse Retro 2.0. We actually ranked them 23rd overall in that tabulation, writing: "The 'goat head' logo loses its magic when stripped away from the red, black and silver color scheme that evoked images of Dominik Hasek saves and Miroslav Satan goals." The sentiment still stands.

No. 22: Calgary Flames

This one gets an "A" for concept alone: an entire jersey commemorating Calgary's final season in the Saddledome. That includes debossing on the sleeves to represent the arena's windows and the roofline being represented on the hem of the sweater. Unfortunately, using the texture of the arena ceiling on the "Flaming C" logo leaves it looking like an ode to breakfast waffles.

No. 23: New Jersey Devils

Is Lou Lamoriello still running this team? After breaking the template with the "Jersey" jerseys, which are now retired, the Devils retreated to what's essentially a black base version of their 2024 Stadium Series jersey. Not a bad-looking jersey at all, but it still feels like a missed opportunity given the team's name -- not to mention there's little "Hometown" in this remix.

No. 24: Winnipeg Jets

The Jets went in an interesting direction with their Hometown Remix sweaters: skyward. These jerseys are inspired by the Aurora Borealis, which can be seen in Winnipeg during the fall and winter. The jet on the crest is supposed to look like it has been lit by the Northern Lights, and the names and numbers are supposed to seem like they're glowing.

Neat idea, even if they're giving "what if we did tie-dye our Connor Hellebuyck jersey we're never wearing again?" energy.

No. 25: Philadelphia Flyers

We want to be kind to these jerseys, because the amount of detail in them is remarkable. The Flyers went with the Liberty Bell as inspiration, drawing everything from the spacing of the jersey's stripes to using the actual inscription on the bell on the sleeves to having a "crack" in their numbers system. But the Flyers are, and ever shall be, the orange and black. Making gray the primary color of a Flyers jersey -- while novel! -- just doesn't fit the motif.

No. 26: Utah Mammoth

The primary logo is Utah's secondary logo: a "U" with a tusk swooping through it. These are fine. What did you think you were getting? Snow kachina?

No. 27: Colorado Avalanche

The Avalanche topped our Reverse Retro 1.0 ranking with their Quebec Nordiques throwback. Their follow-up was less iconic, but a nice-looking sweater that incorporated the state flag. Their Hometown Remix sweater also uses that logo in a "frosted, glistening" ode to the Rocky Mountains. Perfect if you're cosplaying Elsa from "Frozen" as Cale Makar, less so as a specialty jersey.

No. 28: Boston Bruins

The Bruins have had a lot of different jerseys in the past 100 years, including nine different outdoor game looks. At some point, the wells of inspiration run a little dry. So for the Hometown Remix campaign, the team went with, "Hey, Boston sure does have a lot of colleges, huh?" Get one at your local campus bookstore.

No. 29: St. Louis Blues

The Blues have done this logo and look before as a third jersey and they were awesome in a way this one is not. But the real flaws in this Blues Remix sweater are all the forced references to the Mississippi River, from the ripples on the arms to the little wavey lines around the crest. Fanatics said: "Inspired by the dark waters of the Mississippi, black makes a striking appearance as the primary jersey color." OK then.

No. 30: Vancouver Canucks

This is, like, the third or fourth jersey to celebrate "the city after dark" and by far the most ordinary, even with the city skyline on the sleeves. The crest features "a stealth-mode orca in deep blues with shining silver eyes," which sure sounds better than it looks.

No. 31: New York Rangers

The Rangers' specialty jerseys either have some diagonal wordmark or one of two logos they've used since the 1990s. For their Hometown Remix jersey, they have some diagonal wordmark AND one of two logos they've used since the 1990s, in this case the famed Liberty Head.

No. 32: Chicago Blackhawks

Finally, here's an unfortunate manufacturing error in which a Chicago Blackhawks logo was mistakenly stitched onto a Dallas Stars jersey!

Wait, hold on, we're now being told this is the Blackhawks' Hometown Remix jersey.

For the first time, the team will wear a green jersey during games, as their green St. Patrick's Day jerseys were only worn in warmups back in the day. The Chicago flag is represented with four debossed stars on the sleeves to connect it to the city.

Why are the Blackhawks ranked last? Because they play in Chicago, a city with an endless amount of aesthetics and iconography that could make for an instant classic jersey.

This program is supposed to give teams the chance to highlight their locations or bond themselves to something locally iconic. Even if you wanted to make the case that these jerseys celebrate making the river green for St. Patrick's Day, it's still more about a random holiday than the city and its people. Wrestler CM Punk has a deeper connection to Chicago with his wrestling trunks. Use the flag. Use The Bean. Put a picture of Cousin from "The Bear" serving an Italian Beef Sandwich. Have a cow kicking over a lantern on the hem. Anything!

It's a missed opportunity and hopefully a lesson learned for whatever the next jersey program ends up being in the NHL.

stories.headline: Michael Carrick has 'no concerns' over Lisandro Martínez's commitment
stories.summary: Michael Carrick has insisted he's got "no concerns" about Lisandro Martinez's commitment to Manchester United.
stories.body:
Michael Carrick has insisted he's got "no concerns" about Lisandro Martínez's commitment to Manchester United after the defender followed up his criticism of the club's board with a woeful performance against Chelsea.

Martínez was sent off at Stamford Bridge after giving away a penalty which allowed Chelsea to take a 2-0 lead.

In the last month, the Argentina international was also responsible for Tottenham's late equaliser in a 1-1 draw at Old Trafford and criticised director of football Jason Wilcox following the 2-0 defeat to Atlético Madrid.

The 28-year-old is out of contract at the end of the season and there have been suggestions that his behaviour -- on and off the pitch -- is linked to a desire to quit the club.

Carrick, however, has backed Martínez and insists the World Cup winner is determined to get back to his best.

"I've got no concerns about commitment at all," Carrick told a news conference on Tuesday.

"The dressing room is a good, good place. I've said it before, the commitment of the players to the club, to me, to each other is I don't question that at all. We need to play better, we can make better decisions, but commitment's not a thing at all."

Carrick is under severe pressure following a run of nine games without a win.

- Ogden: Why Man United are so bad at hiring managers post-Ferguson

Club bosses are set to evaluate his position during the international break after games against Roma and Aston Villa this week. The 45-year-old's job is on the line, but he's choosing to remain positive ahead of two games which could decide his fate.

"I can look into the future, but you never know what's going to happen," Carrick said.

"That doesn't change how we're preparing for the game tomorrow, and I'm actually really looking forward to the game. I can't wait for the game tomorrow.

"You might think I'm crazy with the results we've had and what's going on, but I really can't wait for the game tomorrow, and that's all I'm focused on. Whatever happens is going to happen after that in whatever direction it goes in, but we want to make it a big night tomorrow night first."

United return to Old Trafford on Tuesday for the first time since the team was booed off after the dismal 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth.

While Carrick was applauded by supporters, the atmosphere changed once he disappeared down the tunnel and only the players were left on the pitch.

Kobbie Mainoo said he understands fans' frustration about how the season has started and admitted the squad need to give them something to shout about against Roma.

"In these tough times you can't expect the fans 100,000% of the time to be happy and cheering when we're not putting out results, you know," Mainoo said.

"We owe it to them to put the results out there for them to cheer again."

- Erik ten Hag: Man United being relegated is 'certainly possible'

stories.headline: Trial begins for Guardians' Emmanuel Clase and Luis Ortiz in pitch-rigging case
stories.summary: The trial of two major league baseball pitchers accused of rigging pitches in a betting scheme begins Monday in federal court in Brooklyn.
stories.body:
The trial of two major league baseball pitchers accused of rigging pitches in a betting scheme begins Monday with jury selection in federal court in New York.

Cleveland Guardians pitchers Emmanuel Clase de la Cruz and Luis Leandro Ortiz Ribera are charged with conspiracy to commit wire and honest services fraud, sports bribery and money laundering.

Co-defendants Robinson Vásquez Germosen and Luis Arismendy Paca Méndez are accused of sharing inside information from Clase, 28, with other bettors and using that information to wager on what federal prosecutors say were predetermined pitches.

Paca Méndez, who prosecutors allege lived with Clase at his house in Ohio during part of the scheme, will not take part in the trial in Brooklyn after being extradited from the Dominican Republic to the U.S. on Oct. 19, according to a spokesperson for the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Eastern District of New York.

Guardians front office personnel, including general manager Mike Chernoff, as well as coaches and catchers who worked with Clase and Ortiz are among the potential witnesses, along with officials from Major League Baseball and DraftKings.

The government alleges that Clase, one of the best closers in baseball, rigged at least 18 pitches in 17 games from May 19, 2023, to May 28, 2025, often by intentionally throwing balls or by tipping off bettors that he would throw an off-speed pitch. Prosecutors say he shared information about the planned result or the velocity of the pitches with bettors, including Vásquez and Méndez, using code words like "rooster" and "chicken," sometimes in exchange for "bribe and kickback payments."

The bettors allegedly placed more than 100 wagers and won at least $400,000 on Clase's pitches. In a hearing Friday, attorneys disclosed that the bets were placed with DraftKings, FanDuel and ESPN BET.

Clase's attorneys have argued that his pitches were part of normal baseball strategy. "At trial, the jury will be tasked with deciding if certain ... pitches were thrown for legitimate, baseball-strategy reasons or in furtherance of a scheme to defraud betting companies," his attorneys wrote in a September filing. "In isolation, any single pitch in the dirt can be painted as nefarious."

In a January filing, Clase's attorneys said that he did not participate in a conspiracy and instead had communicated with his associates about gambling on rooster fighting in the Dominican Republic, where it is legal. They added that Clase and Ortiz moved money to their home country to buy and care for livestock, including a horse.

During the hearing Friday, prosecutors said they recently learned that Clase owes the IRS about $500,000, which they argued showed motive for the alleged bribes. Clase's attorneys denied in court that their client had a financial motive. The judge ruled the information inadmissible for trial.

ESPN obtained records of a federal tax lien listed under Clase's name in Maricopa County, Arizona, for $588,919.60 in back taxes from 2022 to 2024. The lien was issued in May 2026.

Ortiz, 27, is accused of manipulating two pitches in two Guardians games in June 2025, according to the indictment. Prosecutors say Ortiz was in debt to a company that advances money to professional athletes against their future earnings.

In a September filing, Ortiz's attorneys said that he never communicated with the bettors: "Not once. Not by text, not by phone, not in person."

"The government's case against Luis Leandro Ortiz Ribera is remarkably thin," Ortiz's attorneys wrote. "It consists, in essence, of the anticipated testimony of two cooperating bettors ... and a handful of wagers that [they] and two of their relatives placed on two pitches Mr. Ortiz threw."

The alleged scheme came to light after sportsbooks flagged unusual betting interest on Ortiz's first pitch in the bottom of the second inning on June 15, 2025, against the Seattle Mariners, and his first pitch in the top of the third inning against the St. Louis Cardinals on June 27, 2025.

In a court filing, the government said the size of the bets on the two Ortiz pitches was up to "136 times greater" than the average wager placed by the bettors allegedly involved. MLB has since asked sportsbooks to place a maximum $200 betting limit on wagers on individual pitches and to prohibit such bets from being included in parlays.

MLB placed Ortiz and Clase on non-disciplinary paid leave in July 2025. The two were indicted four months later.

Clase earned more than $13 million over a seven-year major league career, and he was scheduled to make $6.4 million in 2026. Ortiz's salary in 2025 was $782,600.

Attorneys for Clase, Ortiz and Paca Méndez did not respond to requests for comment from ESPN. A U.S. Attorney's Office spokesperson declined ESPN's request for comment about the trial.

Vásquez's attorney, Todd Spodek, told ESPN that his client is innocent.

"People forget that an indictment is just the government's side of the story," he said. "Mr. Vásquez is innocent, and we're confident that the evidence will support this."

In court documents filed days before the trial, the prosecution and defense sparred over the translation from Spanish to English of text messages, videos and voice memos that will be used as evidence. A Spanish-language interpreter will participate in the proceedings.

Judge Kiyo A. Matsumoto will oversee the trial, which the government estimates will last three weeks.

The wire fraud, honest services and money laundering charges carry maximum prison sentences of 20 years, while the sports bribery charge has a five-year maximum prison sentence, according to the Department of Justice.

The case is one of five federal sports gambling cases involving alleged performance manipulation by professional or college athletes over the past three years -- and the first to go to trial.

ESPN reporter Michael Rothstein and ESPN researcher John Mastroberardino contributed to this story.

stories.headline: Messi brings Miami back to stun Revs, clinch Champions Cup spot
stories.summary: Inter Miami CF beat the New England Revolution 2-1 on Sunday in Foxborough, Massachusetts, with Lionel Messi once again providing the magic touch, this time to ensure his team's spot in the 2027 Concacaf Champions Cup.
stories.body:
Inter Miami CF beat the New England Revolution 2-1 on Sunday in Foxborough, Massachusetts, with Lionel Messi once again providing the magic touch, this time to ensure his team's spot in the 2027 Concacaf Champions Cup.

The win also helped Miami leapfrog the Revs into second place in the Eastern Conference with one game remaining in the MLS regular season.

"It makes me very happy for the players and for the club, we are on the side of contributing things," Miami manager Cristian González said after the game. "We are at a club that is in continuous growth, I have players committed to us. We needed to win and we challenged ourselves on what kind of team we wanted to be."

The Revolution edged out Inter Miami in the first half, registering six total shots, five corner kicks and generating an expected goals of .75, but the match went to the break tied 0-0.

Dániel Gazdag then opened up the scoring in the initial minutes of the second half, connecting with Ilay Feingold inside the box before finding the back of the net.

Miami found a way to respond to Gazdag's strike with a goal from Germán Berterame -- set up by a deft backward header from Messi -- in the 69th minute. González then bolstered Inter Miami's attack after drawing level, substituting in Luis Suárez, who had started Miami's last 25 games.

"We knew we were going up against a rival that tries to seek out duels where they defend high, so the possibility of changes was to have depth, look for the spaces, and the one-on-one matchups. We struggled with ball possession, which at times was very passive," said González. "My message to the players is I need everyone. In this case, we believed we needed to make some changes.

"This doesn't mean this is the team that's going to start the playoffs. Everyone shows me they're eager to want to play."

Messi doubled the score for Inter Miami, dribbling past defenders outside the box and smashing a trademark low, left-footed shot past Revs keeper Matt Turner.

The Revolution almost found their way back for a draw, but Ian Fray's own goal was quickly ruled offside to let Miami off the hook after it looked like Messi's heroics had been undone.

Ultimately, it was Messi's goal that clinched Inter Miami a spot in the 2027 Champions Cup. Had Miami lost or tied the game against the Revs they would have had work left to do on Decision Day on Nov. 7 to get into North America's top club competition.

"I have no doubt that he's the best of all," González said of Messi. None of them can compare to him when it comes to respect for his colleagues. Leo at his age and what he does, from my point of view, deserves the MVP and also the Ballon d'Or. I hope he can achieve it."

Inter Miami now joins Nashville SC, the Revs and the Vancouver Whitecaps in the 2027 Concacaf Champions Cup. The winner of the 2026 MLS Cup will also have a place in the Champions Cup.

The Herons now have 59 points from 33 games, and will finish the regular season with a home game against Charlotte FC that will have seeding implications ahead of the MLS playoffs.

stories.headline: How the Golden State Valkyries won the 2026 WNBA title in just two years
stories.summary: When Golden State joined the WNBA, the owner said the team would win a title within five years. The Valkyries did it in two.
stories.body:
SAN FRANCISCO -- Almost exactly two years ago, Natalie Nakase sat across from Golden State owner Joe Lacob for her job interview to become the head coach of the WNBA's newest team, the Valkyries. It was October 2024, and Nakase had walked into the interview with notes on why she would be the best fit, her vision for how to build a team and what set her apart from her colleagues.

But the first 10 minutes of the conversation were led by Lacob: He told Nakase he likes to set incredibly high goals and shared how he plans to achieve them. Nakase sat up straighter and leaned in a few inches closer, enticed by Lacob's work ethic.

Near the end of the conversation, Lacob told Nakase the ultimate goal, the same one he had shared in the news conference announcing the creation of the team a year earlier: "We're going to win a championship in five years."

She slammed her fists on the table in front of them.

"Hell yeah, we're gonna win a championship," she said.

On Saturday, the Golden State Valkyries did just that, beating the Atlanta Dream 68-63 in Game 7 of the WNBA Finals to win their first title.

Lacob and Nakase were wrong about one thing, though. The Valkyries didn't win their first championship in five years. They did it in two.

"I walked out of that conversation with Joe like, 'I want to work for him,'" Nakase said. "More than that, I want to win that first championship for him."

After the interview, Nakase immediately called her mentors, asking them how she could deliver on Lacob's aspirations. Their biggest piece of advice was to build a clear culture, and do it with competitors who would sacrifice anything for the group.

Along with general manager Ohemaa Nyanin, Nakase set the identity she wanted for her team: scrappy, defensive-minded, no egos. The Valkyries built the team their way, facing external scrutiny nearly every step of the way. People gawked -- or even laughed -- at Lacob's proclamation. But Nakase stood strong in her belief, and in his.

Sitting next to the championship trophy with a beer in her hand Saturday, Nakase was asked if winning the title felt as she imagined it would.

"F--- yeah."

TOGETHER, NYANIN AND Nakase handpicked the players who make up Golden State's roster. During the 2024 expansion draft, the Valkyries acquired Veronica Burton, the gritty two-way guard, and Kayla Thornton, a reigning WNBA champion -- two cornerstones of the franchise -- as well as Cecilia Zandalasini, an Italian national. Tiffany Hayes, a former Sixth Player of the Year, signed in free agency, and Janelle Salaun, a French forward, signed on a training camp roster. The Valkyries used their No. 5 pick in 2025 on Juste Jocyte -- a 19-year-old from Lithuania who stayed overseas that year.

Again, their decisions were questioned. Without a star, and without a history of any success, external expectations for the Valkyries were low.

But in the 2025 postseason, this group made history, propelling the Valkyries to become the first expansion franchise in WNBA history to make the playoffs in its first season. The Valkyries were swept by the Minnesota Lynx in the first round, but it laid the foundation for what the team could build on, and made Golden State an attractive landing place for free agents.

For more than a year, the Valkyries knew whom they wanted to prioritize. Gabby Williams was part of Nyanin's original vision of the team, and Nakase met with Williams in 2025 in Turkey to pitch her on coming to Golden State. But the Seattle Storm cored Williams that offseason, guaranteeing Seattle exclusive negotiating rights with the French national. Williams remembers when she heard Lacob make his proclamation in 2023. "I was impressed, and I was enticed. It was like, this is a team I could want to play for one day," Williams said. "I thought I would finish my career in Seattle, but hearing that made me think a little bit. This guy is not playing around; he wants to win. That was eye-opening to me."

When Williams became a free agent, the Valkyries contacted her again, and Lacob joined Nakase and Nyanin in the recruitment.

"He said, 'This is why we are going to win. This is why it would be silly for you to go anywhere else. This is why we're going to have longevity. I want to build dynasties here,'" Williams said.

"Who doesn't want to come to something like that? We play this game to win championships. I've never won one, and at this point in my career, that is the top priority. ... I was so convinced that I would not win anywhere else."

One day after signing Williams, the Valkyries made another trajectory-shifting acquisition, landing Kiah Stokes after she spent four seasons and won three titles with Las Vegas, where she played alongside A'ja Wilson every day and under Nakase for one year. After Iliana Rupert announced that she would miss the 2026 season due to pregnancy, Stokes started every game, defending Angel Reese in the Finals.

Nyanin knew that these players could unlock a new level of her team. What has surprised the GM, though, is how quickly it has come together.

"You just never know if that's going to work out," Nyanin said.

It has. Williams, who was named Finals MVP thanks to a 30-point performance in Game 7, is having the best season of her career. She averaged a career-best 14.4 points and shot 34.2% from 3 -- and also finished second in Defensive Player of the Year voting and received WNBA All-Defensive first-team honors. She became the engine for Golden State's top-ranked defense, while also stepping up to be the shotmaker the Valkyries needed.

"The best part has been coming to work every day and enjoying it. Like, actually, that's a huge part of contending," Williams said. "When the playoffs started, our motivation was just -- we didn't want to stop playing together. We wanted to go as deep as we could because we knew this is the last time we could have a group like this. It's been really healing for me. It's made this season really special."

Down late in a win-or-go-home Game 3 in the first round against the Dallas Wings, Thornton pulled Burton, Williams and Kaila Charles into a huddle beneath their basket. They put their arms around each other and took a collective breath.

"It's just one of those things where [it was] an awareness of what we need," Burton said. "And in that moment, we needed to take an exhale and be together and just be present. ... That's pouring into each other and building each other up."

As Nyanin watched from the tunnel -- and as that sigh fueled their comeback and offered a glimpse of the composure Golden State, a team with no All-WNBA player selections, has possessed since its inception, Nyanin knew that all of the pieces she put together fit perfectly.

"That was the epitome of things we have said to them here and there," Nyanin said. "In that moment, all of the little things we have put together, I took a breath as well just to say yes, they will fight with each other and for each other. That's exactly why I am doing the job I am doing."

NAKASE WOULDN'T LET her players pick up a ball for the first three days of training camp this season.

There was no shooting, no running plays, no offense. The first three days of camp were dedicated to defense.

"That's when I knew this was going to be different," Burton said.

Those early sessions set the tone for what Nakase would demand: consistent defensive intensity, attention to detail and execution on the game plan. It also gave her players a taste of the kind of coach she is -- one who plays battle sounds during practice and calls her players "killers," doesn't allow for celebrations, and believes that cursing just means you're telling the truth.

Even when Nakase's behavior seems jarring -- or as she puts it, extreme -- she has built an environment that encourages her players to speak up and feel respected. It's why they so willingly buy into Nakase's vision and style.

"She's so authentic," Williams said. "We know her intentions are to put us in the best position to win. ... She's passionate. And sometimes we laugh at her, but we also check on her ... it's the love we have for each other."

When Williams arrived in Golden State, she told Nakase that sometimes her delivery was confusing. Others have told Nakase that they needed more time to celebrate the smaller wins. Her coaching staff urged her to take more care of herself so she can be a better leader.

All of this experience has led the Valkyries here, to their first title. Nakase's focus on defense made Golden State's unit the top ranked in the league through the regular season -- holding opponents to a league-low 75.1 points per game -- and second best in the playoffs. Stokes had 31 blocked shots this postseason, tied with Lisa Leslie for the most in WNBA history.

And her players' feedback has pushed Nakase to be a better version of herself -- and helped turn around the Finals when Golden State trailed 2-1. After the first three games of the series, she gave herself an F-minus score on her coaching because her communication was poor. So she turned to her players to see how she -- and in turn they -- could be better.

"You can give the best scheme in the world, but if your players don't want to follow it, it's not going to be successful," Stokes said. "Her willingness to listen to us and our ideas about what we think we're best at and what we can do, that's one thing that has jumped out to me; her willingness to adapt to her players."

Heading into Game 4, Nakase inserted Hayes and Kaila Charles into the starting lineup in place of Thornton and Zandalasini, respectively. Charles finished the game with a plus-14, and Hayes added 13 points -- and the change led to a massive momentum shift in the series, with the Valkyries taking the next two games.

"The best thing about our team is no one cares who starts, no one cares," Nakase said. "We can do that because we have a really selfless team, ego-less team."

"She's a great coach for a reason," Charles. "We trust our coach, so whatever she sees, we'll execute."

As Nakase walked out of her first interview with Lacob, she pledged to herself not to let his WNBA team fail. When she began to work alongside Nyanin, she promised her that they wouldn't let each other fail. As she opened up each season with her players, Nakase made sure they had every piece of support they needed.

All of this has led to history, and the Valkyries winning a title far sooner than anyone -- even Lacob -- could have ever predicted.

"Of course this is unbelievable," Lacob said Saturday night as the Valkyries celebrated. "Two years? It's insane."
