Oct. 30: Packers' ground game cause for concern

By Adam Rank

Jordan Love throws multiple touchdown passes. Matthew Golden looks good. I mean, Christian Watson left and arrived back at Lambeau Field from an ambulance in a move that would make Triple H say, "no way this is real." And yet, I get a note from my editor (a Packers fan, mind you) complaining about the (lack of a) Green Bay Packers running game.

I mean, the Milwaukee Brewers just won the World Series, but we need to focus on the Packers' rushing attack? Well, I guess that is the best place to start.

The Packers won the game despite rushing for just 66 yards. They have been held to fewer than 90 rushing yards in all eight games, the club's longest streak in the Super Bowl era. The Packers' 485 rushing yards are the fewest by any team through eight games since the 2019 Bengals. I mean, what in the name of Eddie Lee Ivery is going on here?

The short answer is the offensive line is bad. The playcalling is bad. I mean, you think the guy who favored Dion Lewis over Derrick Henry when he was offensive coordinator in Tennessee was ever going to have a solid running game in Green Bay? It's just the facts.

And it's not going to get much easier in the coming weeks, either. The New England Patriots, Minnesota Vikings and Los Angeles Rams aren't great matchups. It's not until the New Orleans Saints in Week 13 that the schedule softens for Josh Jacobs. If you kept him on your roster all this time, you're likely going to be compelled to start him, but the matchups aren't ideal.

Some other notes from Thursday night:

Love has accounted for multiple touchdowns in all eight games this season, but this was his first game of the season with three touchdown passes. He's a set-and-forget quarterback moving forward. It is wild to think he wasn't drafted as a QB1 this year.
Watson is nearing ace territory this season. He recorded his 12th reception of 20-plus yards, second in the league behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba.
Golden is also a must-start, but he registered two drops Thursday. Love has seen 20 drops by his receivers this season. I feel like that total would double if you counted the number of interceptions that are dropped. Or maybe it just seems that way to me, a Bears supporter.
Is the "Bryce Young as a QB1" era over already? Well, for starters, the Carolina Panthers need to do a better job of protecting him. He was hit. A lot. I'm not rushing him back into my lineup next week against the Denver Broncos. You might want to take a look at the waiver wire right now for a streamable option if Young is your only quarterback. Kyler Murray against the Buffalo Bills next week could do the trick.
Chuba Hubbard was good, however. He scored a touchdown, rushed for 81 yards and caught seven balls for 38 more yards. Again, playing the Bills next week makes him a prime RB1.

stories.headline: How NBA title, MVP race has become wide open in two weeks
stories.summary: The NBA season is still young, but injuries and surprising developments have already changed narratives.
stories.body:
The 2026-27 NBA season was projected to be abnormally competitive, as previously rebuilding teams turned the corner and new draft lottery rules gave all 30 franchises an incentive to win.

At the top of the standings, though, three juggernaut rosters towered above the rest: the Oklahoma City Thunder and San Antonio Spurs, who both won more than 60 games before clashing in a seven-game conference finals last season, and the defending champion New York Knicks, who reeled off arguably the most dominant stretch in NBA history en route to the title.

Those three teams were excellent last season, and they returned 14 of their combined 15 starters this fall. So even as the rest of the league's floor rose, the highest ceilings still appeared to reside in New York City and the Southwest.

But surprising developments have changed that narrative less than two weeks into the new season and challenged the triumvirate's hegemony atop the league. Most importantly, a wave of injuries to star players already has altered the league's most important races.

Jump to a section:

How title odds have shifted

The injured stars so far

Is the MVP race wide open?

Scuffling preseason favorites
Oklahoma City opened its season with a firm statement of intent, with 12-point wins over the Spurs and Nuggets -- possibly the Thunder's closest competition in the West.

Then disaster struck. Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace both suffered potentially season-ending injuries in the same game, and Alex Caruso sprained his right ankle the following night. At the same time, Chet Holmgren suffered a patellar tendon tear in his right knee, which will sideline him for at least two months

So Oklahoma City has played its past couple games without four of its top six players, to predictable results: a 24-point loss in Dallas followed by a 21-point loss in Houston. The Thunder were outscored in all eight quarters across those two defeats.

The team will theoretically improve from their current doldrums once Caruso and Holmgren return, but the Thunder are in deep trouble on the perimeter without Williams and Wallace. They look far away from meaningful contention given their horrid spate of injuries.

But Oklahoma City isn't the only preseason favorite with more concerns now than two weeks ago. The Knicks are 2-4 and needed two big comebacks against Detroit and Chicago just to pick up their two wins. And the Spurs started a comparatively better 4-2, but they've looked out of sorts against the toughest competition they've faced and needed overtime to beat the injury-wracked Jazz.

It's very early, and those teams still have plenty of time to round into their best shape. But the title race already looks more open.

According to preseason projections by ESPN's Basketball Power Index (BPI), the Thunder and Spurs combined for a 50% championship probability. Add in the Knicks at 8%, and BPI gave those three favorites a roughly three-fifths chance to win the title. Yet their combined odds have since fallen to just 38%, and that's with the assumption that Wallace and Holmgren return before the playoffs.

Meanwhile, a series of second-tier contenders have started strong, which should increase their confidence that they can close the gap to the Thunder, Spurs and Knicks. The Rockets lead the way with a 5-1 record including wins over Oklahoma City and San Antonio. And in the Eastern Conference, the 76ers, Pistons and Celtics started a combined 16-3 -- meaning those three teams have fewer combined losses than the Knicks have by themselves.

That trend also serves as an argument for teams with strong rosters and ample draft assets, such as Houston and Detroit, to seriously consider making in-season trades with an eye on the Finals.

If the Thunder, Spurs and Knicks were all fully healthy and running roughshod over everyone in their paths, there might be some merit to the idea of keeping one's powder dry rather than making futile trades to try to catch the leading contenders. But if those teams still look more vulnerable than expected in a few months, the deadline could pack a more potent punch.

Even more injuries
Other prospective contenders have also borne the brunt of early-season injuries -- though none to the extent of Oklahoma City's nightmare.

Players who have already missed multiple games this season include Williams, Wallace, Caruso, Holmgren, Coby White, Kon Knueppel, Cameron Johnson, Jalen Duren, Alperen Sengun, Tyrese Haliburton, Ivica Zubac, Anthony Edwards, Paolo Banchero, Jalen Suggs, Kawhi Leonard and Jaren Jackson Jr.

That's more than a full roster's worth of stars (or star role players) who have suffered injuries within the first two weeks of the new season.

Discussion around the league generally points to increased pace and stress on the body as a reason for these injuries, while understanding that they're a mix of soft tissue problems and flukes -- like the collisions that sidelined Williams and Wallace.

It's also clear that there are no quick fixes. The NBA isn't slowing down, and more radical proposals that would change the sport to reduce wear and tear -- from a shorter schedule to 40-minute games -- are equally unlikely to happen any time soon. The injury issue is a figurative pain point for the league and a literal pain point for the players who keep getting hurt.

A (potentially) wide-open MVP race
Looking ahead to the remaining five months of the regular season, it's not just the title race that has opened to new challengers. The MVP race could also devolve into a free-for-all with one more injury.

The two most recent MVPs, who have finished first and second in the voting in some order three years running, have scuffled to start this season, with numbers well below their recent norms. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Nikola Jokic perennially rank among the most productive, efficient stars in the league, but both have looked surprisingly mortal in the early going.

Put another way, Jokic and Gilgeous-Alexander finished first and second in player efficiency rating in each of the past two seasons, and they ranked first and third in 2023-24. Jokic has led the league in PER six years in a row.

Now, Jokic ranks 24th and Gilgeous-Alexander is 16th among qualified players in PER two weeks into this season.

Of course, these comparisons come after a very small sample of play -- but even then, the stars' relative struggles are unusual. Jokic, for instance, just completed his worst five-game stretch (as measured by box plus-minus) at any point in the season since 2020, before he won his first MVP.

For Gilgeous-Alexander, the Thunder's injury issues could counterintuitively give him a better chance to win his third straight MVP. Two-time winners are typically penalized -- if only unconsciously -- by voter fatigue, as no player has won three in a row since Larry Bird in the mid-'80s. However, if Gilgeous-Alexander can keep the Thunder near the top of the Western Conference standings and post his typically exemplary statistics without as much help from teammates, then he'd have a narrative boost to overcome that bias.

Yet if he and Jokic don't live up to the incredibly high standards they set while winning multiple MVPs apiece, then it seems far-fetched to think that either could claim another trophy this season.

That leaves Victor Wembanyama as the clear favorite, and betting odds reflect that status. He's responded by playing at an MVP level so far.

But remember, Wembanyama reached only the bare minimum number of games to qualify for awards last season, and he missed out in 2024-25. If he falls short of 65 games again, he could leave behind a truly wide-open race, with a whole host of viable second-tier candidates suddenly receiving real MVP consideration.

Could Luka Doncic finally receive his long-awaited MVP moment? Could Cade Cunningham, Jayson Tatum or Jalen Brunson become the first Eastern Conference perimeter players to win MVP since LeBron James in Miami? Could 19-year-old Cooper Flagg make a play at an historic award? (The answer is yes if he keeps dominating like he did in his first five games.)

The result is a season that brims with tremendous possibility -- even more than already seemed to be the case when the new year tipped off in October.

stories.headline: 'Integrity, loyalty, respect' - Kimi Antonelli 'represents modern F1 drivers,' says Mercedes boss
stories.summary: Toto Wolff still sees Kimi Antonelli as the "same kid" who joined Mercedes aged 12 and says the new world champion is a role model for all Formula 1 drivers.
stories.body:
Toto Wolff still sees Kimi Antonelli as the "same kid" who joined Mercedes aged 12 and says the new world champion is a role model for all Formula 1 drivers.

Antonelli claimed his place in history as the youngest F1 world champion with third place in Mexico City on Sunday -- clinching the title with four rounds remaining.

As he leapt out of the car, the emotional 20-year-old was embraced by his parents and younger sister Maggie before receiving a huge bear hug from Mercedes boss Wolff.

The 54-year-old has helped nurture Antonelli in the Mercedes programme, from being signed as a karting superstar to now realising his destiny in just his second season in the sport.

"For me, when he was there in the garage at the age of 11, it seems like a few years ago, not seven or eight years," Wolff said.

"Because he's still a kid. We see this world champion in him and the maturity that he has shown.

"But all of us that have been on this journey ... I still see the same kid.

"He hasn't even changed visually a lot. It's so refreshing. I tried to get hold of him a few weeks ago and said 'where's Kimi?,' Kimi, for his birthday, is in the waterpark!"

Antonelli was chosen to replace seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton when he announced his move to Ferrari in 2024, after 12 years and six titles with the team.

Then only 18, it was a big call from Wolff but he maintains he knew instantly that Antonelli was the right replacement.

"When Lewis came to my house that morning, I obviously knew what was happening. The moment he confirmed that he was going to Ferrari, it was instinctive -- I knew that Kimi is going to go in the car," Wolff added.

- The families that built Kimi Antonelli, F1 world champion

- How Kimi Antonelli overcame George Russell, Ferrari to become F1's youngest champion

- Kimi Antonelli is F1 champion. But why didn't he get his trophy in Mexico City?

Antonelli was held aloft on the Mexico podium by Hamilton and Max Verstappen -- two drivers with 11 world championships between them.

The Italian's youthful exuberance shines through his driving and his interviews. The tearful Bologna-born driver spoke passionately about the support of his family and the team having realised his dream.

As Wolff's post-race media session concluded, he asked to make one more comment.

"I discussed it with Mohammed [Ben Sulayem, FIA president] actually," he began.

"This notion of win at all costs. Selfish, opportunistic, ruthless for your own benefit.

"That model of racing driver has died. We have a new champion that represents values like humility, integrity, loyalty, respect. That should be a role model for many other young drivers in junior formulas.

"And should be a role model for the few entitled ones in Formula 1 -- the endless moaners on the radio, the ones that complain, the ones that crash.

"Look at this kid of 20 years and then think what you can do in order to improve.

"That is modern Formula 1. Kimi represents the modern Formula 1 driver because of those values.

"The talent is there with everyone. But you've got to be a good person too. He has demonstrated that you can beat everyone out there by being a good person."

There are four races of the season remaining, starting with next week's round in Brazil -- home of Antonelli's racing hero Ayrton Senna.

The Italian vowed that the title win was just the beginning and Wolff is certain there are more to come.

He added: "I believe that if we give him the car, he's going to be in the hunt for more titles. This was the first today. There will be more."

stories.headline: NHL unveils Hometown Remix jerseys, merchandise for all 32 teams for 2026-27
stories.summary: The NHL revealed the Hometown Remix jerseys for all 32 teams on Monday. The teams will wear these jerseys several times during the 2026-27 regular season.
stories.body:
The NHL Hometown Remix jerseys will be the highest-grossing merchandise program that the league has ever had, according to projections by Fanatics.

All 32 teams revealed their new alternate jerseys on Monday morning, after weeks of buzzing fans scouring the internet for leaks and speculation. The design details draw on local landmarks, culture and tradition, while also nodding to classic looks from the franchises' history.

The Hometown Remix program will run for only one season, with teams wearing their uniforms several times in the 2026-27 regular season. In total, there will be 261 games that feature a Hometown Remix uniform, including 19 games in which both teams will wear their new gear head-to-head.

Brian Jennings, NHL chief branding officer, agreed that this collection of jerseys, hats, jackets and other merchandise could end up being the most lucrative the league has had for a "power of 32" campaign.

"There is a big commercial swing here, and it shows the potential when you do these things and do them right -- bringing strategically aligned retailers, along with our 32 member clubs under the tent early -- you have the potential to make something as meaningful as this. So, we're hoping that it's going to do all of that and more," he said.

Fanatics became the official outfitter of on-ice uniforms and authentic jerseys in the 2024-25 season, signing a 10-year contract with the NHL after its run with Adidas ended. It was expected that Fanatics would spend a couple of seasons making sure the in-game gear was up to standards before attempting any kind of "all 32" jersey program -- something their market research found fans were hungry to see the NHL do again.

The challenge for Fanatics: Finding a jersey campaign that could stand apart from the widely popular Reverse Retro series that Adidas put out in 2020 and 2022, remixing a franchise's previous looks in a spectrum of bold colors.

"We knew we didn't want to do a Reverse Retro 3.0. We wanted to create our own narrative, our own point of view," said Dom Fillion, vice president of creative, design and innovation for Fanatics.

Jennings said the first few concepts from Fanatics were "not ready for primetime" but something clicked with the "hyper local" inspiration for what would become the Hometown Remix jerseys.

Jennings said that the bookings for Hometown Remix jerseys are "four times" larger than they were for the second Reverse Retro jersey campaign.

Other sports have used similar local inspiration, like the NBA's "City Edition" and MLB's "City Connect" jerseys. Jennings said this "was a lane that hockey hadn't taken before," and that the complexities of NHL sweaters gave designers a more interesting canvas on which to create.

Among the notable jerseys in the Hometown Remix program:

Florida Panthers: Inspired by the sunrise in Sunrise, Florida, the Panthers' Remix sweater marks the first time an NHL team has a jersey with pink (or coral) as its primary base color. "We play hockey in South Florida, so there's just a lot of things that probably, in the traditional hockey lexicon, are just not natural," said Mike White, the Panthers' president of business operations, told ESPN.

Philadelphia Flyers: An ode to the Liberty Bell, with a jersey whose striping matches the iconic tourist attraction and that features the Bell's iconic inscription written on the sleeves. The hem of the jersey references America's 250th birthday.

Pittsburgh Penguins: While not explicitly inspired by Pittsburgh native Andy Warhol, this ode to pop art is a colorfully bold take on the Penguins' current jersey. Fillion said it "took some rounds" with the team before the pop art angle came up. "There's a storytelling area that's been heavily indexed within Pittsburgh," he said. "So, they wanted to take this opportunity to create something very different and to really kind of tell a narrative that hasn't been told in the past."

San Jose Sharks: Along with a revamped logo, the sleeves of the sweater are encircled by shark jaws. "An iconic part of [their arena] is the shark head that the team skates out of," Fillion said. "It's definitely a forward kit, but this is exactly what Hometown Remix is about."

Something else that defined the Hometown Remix program were leaks. Over two dozen images of the actual jerseys or graphical recreations of what they looked like were passed around by hockey fans on social media platforms before the release.

"It can feel like a gut punch. You put 18 months of work into this, and somebody starts to opine on two-dimensional artwork and starts to question everything about it," Jennings said. "The design consideration and markers that have gone into this program are extraordinary. I know fans won't like every single one, but they are absolutely phenomenal and I can't wait for the best players in the world to wear them under the spotlight and on the ice where you see the whole uniform system."

The Hometown Remix jerseys hit the ice for the time on Monday night, as the Panthers, Sharks and Chicago Blackhawks wear their new kits.

stories.headline: Noni Madueke: Alexis Mac Allister tried to 'bait me' into red card
stories.summary: Noni Madueke has said that Alexis Mac Allister tried to "bait" him into getting a red card during Arsenal's 1-0 win over Liverpool at Anfield.
stories.body:
Noni Madueke has said that Alexis Mac Allister tried to "bait" him into getting a red card during Arsenal's 1-0 win over Liverpool at Anfield.

The Argentine midfielder went to ground while he and Madueke were face-to-face in the 79th minute of the match and Madueke was not punished.

Speaking to reporters after the match, Madueke said that he didn't think there was "anything" in the incident.

"To be honest, I don't think it's anything -- a yellow card or a red card. The referee didn't think that, VAR [Video Assistant Referee] didn't think that, so we all agreed there," the Arsenal forward said.

"It's a natural movement and he's obviously clever, he tried to bait me into getting a red card there but obviously no. In my head, I was thinking it's possible [to be sent off] with VAR, with whoever interprets it -- I don't know what they're thinking... But thankfully it wasn't."

The Gunners claimed victory at Anfield for the first time in 14 years as Kai Havertz scored the only goal of the game.

Mac Allister was criticised by Jamie Carragher for his role in the incident between himself and Madueke

On Sky Sports, Carragher said: "I am delighted [Madueke] never got sent off there. "We have got to be strong in calling people out and saying 'this is embarrassing.'

"It has got to stop, it's ridiculous. I can't stand it.

"If someone puts their head back then butts, of course it's a red card. But this stuff about a head-to-head, and if someone touches the other one goes down and it's a red card?

- Arsenal hold on for a big win at Liverpool, one Iraola & Co. can learn from

- Declan Rice tops Premier League assist chart - without set-pieces

- Dominik Szoboszlai asks if Liverpool expected to 'dive' to win penalty

"As a game, as football, people in the Premier League and supporters [must] call your own people out for it.

"I am a Liverpool fan and that's a joke from Mac Allister. It's got to stop.

"People are trying to game the system because they know that they can. Red cards are being given for it.

"Whether it's from Howard Webb, the Premier League, the managers -- stop getting red cards for this."

stories.headline: Barcelona's Anthony Gordon ahead of Aston Villa: 'I can do a lot more'
stories.summary: Anthony Gordon said Barcelona have not seen the best of him yet as he promises to become more selfish ahead of Tuesday's Champions League game vs. Aston Villa.
stories.body:
BARCELONA -- Anthony Gordon said Barcelona have not seen the best of him yet as he promises to become more selfish ahead of Tuesday's Champions League game against Aston Villa at Spotify Camp Nou.

Gordon, a €70 million summer signing from Newcastle United, has made an encouraging start to life at Barça, scoring three goals and providing five assists so far.

The England international's most recent goal came in Saturday's 6-1 victory over Alavés, a lovely dinked finish over the goalkeeper, but he says there is more to come as he prepares to face Premier League opposition for the first time since moving to Spain.

"I have started quite well considering it's a new country for me, maybe 7.5 out of 10," he said in a news conference on Monday.

"It's a massive change. It's a new team, although the new country is the biggest part. I have started well, but I can do a lot more.

"It will take some time for me to really settle and grow. When this happens, you will see the very best of me, which you definitely haven't seen so far."

To reach the next level, Gordon says he is aware he must be more selfish at times.

"My demands are always the same, to score, to assist, to be someone who can change a game in any moment and to take responsibility for the game," he said.

"The best in history do this, so that is what I chase. I think I can do it more, be more selfish sometimes, dribble and shoot more. This is the big focus -- definitely to score more goals.

"The challenge here at Barça is different to what I had before. At Everton, I was fighting relegation, which was tough; Newcastle's [objective] was [to quality for the] Champions League or to push up the table.

"Now it's trophies, so three very different challenges. I have really enjoyed all three. To be competing on every front, for every trophy, is definitely the most enjoyable.

"People think that is more pressure, but it's better pressure than fighting relegation or trying to climb the table."

During a recent international break, Gordon suggested he has gained a newfound respect back in his native England after moving to Barcelona in the summer.

However, he wanted to clarify that he did not mean people had a negative opinion of in his homeland, just that Barça's style of play gives him the chance to showcase other attributes.

"When I said that, I didn't mean people were judging me wrong," he said.

"I meant they had never seen me in a system that highlights these qualities. Like I said before, I have played in three different styles of team; that probably shows the intelligence I am talking about to be able to succeed in all three.

"I wasn't saying people judge me wrong or have a negative perspective of me, just that they hadn't seen me in this kind of system before, which I think now is helping them appreciate me a little bit more."

Barça's rout of Alavés at the weekend was a return to winning ways after back-to-back losses to Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid.

Those defeat have raised some doubts about Hansi Flick's team in big games ahead of a week which will see them face Villa and then Atlético Madrid, but Gordon believes the LaLiga leaders can compete with anyone.

"I don't think PSG or Madrid are above us," he insisted. "We have to take responsibility for both losses. They are the two biggest games this season so far and we lost.

"But they are not above us. We are fantastic and on our day can beat anyone."

Next up for Gordon is Unai Emery's Villa, who have won all three of their Champions League games this season, leaving them three points ahead of Barça in the standings heading into Tueday's meeting.

"They are a very good team," Gordon said. "I played against them a couple of times with mixed success.

"They have a great coach [Emery], one of the best in the world right now. They are on a great run as of late. It's a tough challenge, but I am very excited."

stories.headline: MLB offseason buzz: Intel on Skubal, free agency, trade rumors
stories.summary: Who could land Tarik Skubal? Which ace could be traded? Here's the latest as the hot stove ignites.
stories.body:
The MLB hot stove season has arrived!

With players becoming free to sign with any team they choose today (free agency officially begins Monday at 5 p.m. ET), we asked our MLB reporters to open their notebooks with all of the intel they collected from execs, agents and other baseball insiders during the 2026 MLB postseason.

What is the early word on top free agent Tarik Skubal? Would the Tampa Bay Rays trade ace Drew Rasmussen on the heels of their World Series run? What will the New York Yankees, Los Angeles Dodgers and Chicago Cubs do after their playoff exits? And which other teams are generating the most buzz across the industry?

Here is what we're hearing as the hot stove ignites.

What are you hearing about Tarik Skubal as his free agency begins?

Jeff Passan: Skubal is far and away the best player in this class, and the expectation is he will sign before the Dec. 1 lockout. The two most obvious suitors are the two teams with the highest payrolls in baseball: The Los Angeles Dodgers and New York Mets. There are bound to be others. The Chicago Cubs badly want Skubal. They also are skeptical that they will be willing to compete at the sort of dollars Skubal is expected to get -- well in excess of $300 million, potentially in the $400 million-plus range. With Michael King and Nick Pivetta being free agents, the San Diego Padres need a rotation anchor, and arguably the best pitcher in baseball would more than suffice.

Others will join the foray, at the very least showing interest and perhaps joining the bidding. Either way, coming off another excellent season, Skubal will set a new record for a starting pitcher contract. The only question is how big it will be.

Alden Gonzalez: All things being equal -- and by "all things" I, of course, mean "money" -- my sense is Skubal would love to return to the Dodgers. He truly seemed to relish his 2½ months in Los Angeles. He loved the culture, particularly being among so many established, veteran players who were singularly focused on winning. He became besties with Blake Snell, was awed by the organization's resources and, overall, seemed to fit in seamlessly. But it's going to come down to price. And whether the Dodgers would be willing to match Steve Cohen's Mets or any other suitors that materialize given the threat of a salary cap remains to be seen.

Which other free agents are generating the most early buzz?

Buster Olney: Skubal is a market of one -- I've had a couple of folks estimate he'll get something north of Yoshinobu Yamamoto, in a six- or seven-year deal, with the usual suspects bidding against each other -- but behind him is a range of good veteran starting pitchers who will come off the board before the lockout.

Michael King, Clay Holmes, Nick Martinez and Tyler Mahle are among the starters who probably will have offers to accept, if they choose to wrap up their negotiations in November, because they're all in line to have good short-term compensation that teams can absorb no matter what financial system is in place next year. The playoffs and World Series served as a one month-long advertisement for Martinez, because not only did he pitch well and take the ball on short rest, but so much was said about how his clubhouse presence was difference-making for the Rays.

Seiya Suzuki might have the most leverage of the position players to sign, given that he's a right-handed power bat in a market starved for players like him.

Jesse Rogers: There were a slew of starters who were moved at the deadline in need of new homes now that they're free agents. Rays star Freddy Peralta likely improved his position in the market more than anyone considering his performance in Tampa. The same could be said of Padres righty Michael King who pitched his best in the postseason as well.

Neither of those players can receive a qualifying offer, making them even more attractive to teams, and they headline a group of starters who should sign before a December lockout.

Who are the biggest trade candidates this offseason?

Olney: The trade market really won't gain clarity until after the next CBA is settled, except in a few isolated cases; I've heard Seattle is poking around to assess how its surplus in pitching might be used to add a bat. But generally, teams are going to be very wary of making trades without being able to attach appropriate value to the players proposed in deals -- and no one will be able to do that with confidence until they know what the financial system looks like.

Passan: At the top of the list is Tampa Bay ace Drew Rasmussen, whose $20 million salary would push the Rays' payroll above their 2026 level without making another move. Will their World Series run encourage ownership to push the payroll and keep Rasmussen around for another run, or is the ability to clean up in a trade too strong to turn down?

The Astros, under new GM Randy Flores, have to decide what to do with shortstop Jeremy Pena a year before he reaches free agency. Multiple candidates for the GM job had suggested a rebuild would be the best course of action. The Los Angeles Angels, after trading Jose Soriano at the deadline, still have left-hander Reid Detmers and shortstop Zach Neto -- and the new head of baseball operations there has a mess to clean up. Arizona could move Ketel Marte -- if he's willing to waive his no-trade clause. And while William Contreras isn't going anywhere even though he is nearing free agency, the World Series champion Brewers will at least listen on closer Trevor Megill.

What are you hearing the pending lockout could mean for the pace of offseason moves?

Jorge Castillo: The expectation is it's going to be 2021 all over again. Five years ago, the last few days of November were a frenzy as teams committed $1.9 billion to free agents before the previous collective bargaining agreement expired. Nine players signed nine-figure contracts, led by Corey Seager's 10-year, $325 million deal with the Texas Rangers.

While Tarik Skubal, the top free agent this winter, is expected to sign a deal north of that before the lockout, this free agent class isn't nearly as deep. Players are going to fly off the board anyway.

Gonzalez: Ditto on the amount of action, and, to emphasize: the perception among executives is that this is generally a very weak crop of free agents. Outside of Teruaki Sato, a 27-year-old Japanese third baseman who's expected to be posted in the coming days and could one day be a Triple Crown threat, it's slim pickings on offense.

Aside from Skubal, the best starting pitcher available might be Kaima Taira, a 5-foot-8 right-hander with a vast repertoire. The markets for Sato, Taira and fellow Japanese star Hiromi Itoh will dominate a lot of the conversation over these next few weeks. But there will be a lot of action around them.

Has a Rays-Brewers World Series impacted how teams are approaching the offseason?

Passan: Not really. The Rays and Brewers have been regarded as excellent organizations for the last decade. Getting to the World Series is validation, yes, but their approaches are well-known and have been for years. Teams with more resources aren't suddenly going to give away the advantage that accompanies higher payrolls simply because the Rays, Brewers and Cleveland Guardians found success with lower ones. If the demand for players who put the ball in play or are elite baserunners rise precipitously, sure, we'll entertain the idea that there's some sort of an effect. But we'll take the under.

Rogers: It's too early to tell, but there is some chatter about the way those teams put the ball in play having a ripple effect in the sport. If anything, they serve as a reminder that there is more than one way to win a game and the more diverse options you have at the plate or on the mound, the better. Winning without just slugging home runs has taken some notice around the league.

What are the Dodgers most likely to do in the offseason after being dethroned this postseason?

Gonzalez: Outside of a pursuit of Skubal and a restocking of their bullpen -- Alex Vesia and Evan Phillips are among their free agents, and the Dodgers will probably be interested in a reunion -- there might not be a whole lot. Even without Skubal, the Dodgers possess enviable pitching depth.

Their entire starting lineup is under contract. And though their front office will spend a lot of time debating the merits of a younger position-player group, that might ultimately happen internally -- with the likes of Josue De Paula, Alex Freeland and, when he recovers from elbow surgery, Dalton Rushing mixing in. Could a blockbuster deal for a young, controllable, upper-eschelon position player materialize? Certainly. But those are always difficult.

Olney: The postseason demonstrated that the Dodgers have to start thinking about reshaping their position player group, to get younger and more athletic. But that will be challenging, with so many of their veterans under contract. The most obvious trade candidate in their position player group is Teoscar Hernandez, because as he gets older and his defensive skills naturally decline, there is no out for him at the DH spot, with the presence of Shohei Ohtani.

After both seasons ended short of where they hoped, how are the two New York teams likely to approach the offseason?

Castillo: The Mets will be the more aggressive of the two clubs, and it starts with Tarik Skubal. They are considered the favorite to land the prize of this free agent class for two reasons: (A) there's a clear need for a top-tier starting pitcher, (B) they're one of the very few teams willing to pay top dollar for premier free agents.

The Yankees have a few decisions to make. Closer David Bednar is a free agent. They'll likely look for an upgrade at third base. Jazz Chisholm Jr. and Trent Grisham are as good as gone so they'll need to figure out center field and second base. But there are internal options for all those uncertainties.

The Yankees believe they have a championship contender with a few tweaks. The Mets, after missing the playoffs consecutive seasons, are still laying the foundation.

Passan: Both have work to do. The back end of the Yankees' bullpen is nearly empty, second and third base are unclear and while the Yankees have more offensive talent than most, finding spots for them leaves the team vulnerable defensively. The Yankees will be good again because of their starting pitching and star bats, but getting to a championship level will necessitate more.

The Mets just want to get back to the playoffs, and they've got a handful of pieces capable of getting them there. Signing Skubal would be a great place to start. Beyond that, they need significant bullpen help, another starting arm and two more productive bats to be able to say they're on the level of the Braves and Phillies, let alone the Marlins and Nationals, both of whom took steps forward in 2026.

Which other teams does the industry think could make a splash this winter?

Olney: The Cubs, Mariners and Padres -- flush with new owner cash -- and after the lockout, the Angels. The Cubs have a group of veterans in their lineup who are win-now players, like Alex Bregman, Dansby Swanson, Nico Hoerner and Michael Busch, and they need to match that by enhancing their pitching. The question with so many teams is whether or not their respective owners will green-light moves -- I've heard estimates of anywhere from 12 to 18 teams will be largely inclined to sit out November, but of course, that could change if front offices successfully lobby for adding payroll before the lockout.

Rogers: Almost by definition, the Cubs have to be active -- otherwise they won't be able to field a pitching staff. With several pitchers coming off injuries and a bunch of free agent arms, the Cubs need bodies. They'll entertain almost anyone which also means circling back to some of their own guys. Clay Holmes and David Peterson could be candidates for a return engagement. Some believe the Mariners will also do some reshaping of their roster after such a down year.

stories.headline: Messi tracker: Goals, assists, key moments in 2026
stories.summary: ESPN provides game-by-game analysis of Lionel Messi's performances for Inter Miami and Argentina.
stories.body:
Lionel Messi will aim for more success in 2026. His Inter Miami side captured its first MLS Cup title last season and will look to defend it -- and add further silverware too -- in its first season at Nu Stadium, the club's new home.

Messi also captained Argentina as they fell just one step short of defending their FIFA World Cup crown, losing 1-0 in extra time to Spain in the final of what could be his last tournament.

As the 39-year-old continues to feature for both club and country, ESPN will track his performances game-by-game, providing stats and analysis each time he pulls on a Herons or Albiceleste jersey.

Messi's 2026 tally:

Games played: 46
Goals: 41
Assists: 19

Nov. 1: New England Revolution 1-2 Inter Miami

Messi once again provided the magic touch for Miami, this time to ensure his team's spot in the 2027 Concacaf Champions Cup.

The Herons' marquee star set up a goal and scored the winner as Miami leapfrogged New England into second place in the Eastern Conference with one game remaining in the MLS regular season.

After going behind to a Dániel Gazdag goal, Miami responded with a strike from Germán Berterame -- set up by a deft backward header from Messi -- before the 39-year-old scored the winner in the 83rd minute. Sumptuous stuff.

Oct. 28: FC Cincinnati 2-2 Inter Miami
No goals or assists for Messi in what was an eventful 2-2 draw with FC Cincinnati on Wednesday night.

Luis Suárez scored in the 61st minute to give Miami a 1-0 lead, and then the reigning MLS Cup champions needed some late-game heroics to salvage a point. They still fell to third in the Eastern Conference, after New England beat Red Bull New York 3-2 on Wednesday.

Oct. 24: Red Bull New York 2-0 Inter Miami
It has been an eventful few days for Messi. Just a day before the match, he traveled to Spain to receive the 2026 Princess of Asturias Award for Sports, becoming the first individual soccer player to earn the honor.

He then returned to the United States and joined his teammates in New Jersey, starting on the bench before coming on in the 56th minute. However, he was unable to make an impact as the hosts secured a 2-0 victory, ending Miami's three-game winning streak.

Oct. 17: Atlanta United 1-3 Inter Miami
Messi scored twice in four minutes as Miami won 3-1 in Atlanta.

After Germán Berterame opened the scoring just before halftime, Messi doubled Miami's lead in the 56th minute, exchanging passes with Berterame before weaving past a defender and firing a low left-footed shot into the net.

Messi struck again in the 60th minute, latching on to a pass from Luis Suárez before beating his marker and slotting past goalkeeper Lucas Hoyos. The brace took Messi's MLS-leading tally to 25 goals for the season, while Miami extended its winning streak to three matches.

Oct. 14: Inter Miami 2-0 NYCFC
No goals, but after a scoreless first half, Messi helped break the deadlock by setting up Rodrigo De Paul for the opening goal. Germán Berterame later doubled Miami's advantage as the Herons secured their second consecutive win and clinched a spot in the MLS playoffs.

Oct. 10: Inter Miami 4-0 D.C. United

Back in the pink of Inter Miami, and back in the goals for Messi.

His two strikes sealed an emphatic 4-0 win for the Herons over D.C. United at Nu Stadium on Saturday night.

After Luis Suárez had Miami 2-0 up after 39 minutes Messi scored his first in the 47th, retrieving a pass from the Uruguayan before tapping in a shot inside the right post.

Messi then padded the hosts' lead in the 60th minute, latching on to Rodrigo De Paul's pass, before dribbling inside the area, eluding two United defenders and firing past goalkeeper Sean Johnson with a shot from 12 yards.

Oct. 6: Argentina 3-0 Benin

It was an emotionally charged night in Buenos Aires as Messi played his final international match for Argentina, the team that he had led to World Cup glory and two Copa América titles as captain.

The friendly match at the Estadio Monumental was goalless at halftime, but just a few minutes after the break Messi's in-swinging corner from the left was rattled home on the volley by Nicolás Otamendi.

Then, on the hour mark, Messi spotted Nico Paz in space 25 yards from goal. He fed a square pass with the outside of his boot to the Como player, who curled in a classy finish.

But the night undoubtedly belonged to Messi, and he fired a penalty into the top corner to cap off his 208th and final senior appearance for his country with his 126th goal.

Sep. 27: Columbus Crew 2-1 Inter Miami
Before heading to Argentina for his final international match, Messi gave Miami fans something to savor in Ohio.

From a set piece wide on the right wing and with most of those in the stadium, including those in the Columbus defense, surely expecting a cross, Messi's left foot sent the ball curling wickedly into the far top corner of the net.

Messi had chances to add to that tally in the second half but was denied from distance by Columbus goalkeeper Patrick Schulte and put another effort into the side netting.

Then Jamal Thiaré scored in the eighth minute of second-half stoppage time to give the Columbus Crew a stunning 2-1 win.

Sep. 20: Inter Miami 2-2 San Diego FC

Messi's sublime curling free kick was not enough to inspire the Herons to a win against San Diego on Sunday night.

After falling behind to an Anders Dreyer goal in the 12th minute, 39-year-old Messi levelled the scores with beautiful set-piece shot in the 24th minute. His well-hit effort evaded a number of attackers and defenders before sneaking in at the far post.

Miami thought they'd won the match after Luiz Suarez fired the hosts ahead in the 74th minute, only for Dreyer to nab his second goal of the game and ensure the points were shared.

Sep. 16: Inter Miami 2-0 Cruz Azul

Another day, another trophy for Messi.

The Argentine master scored his 100th goal for Inter Miami as the Herons defeated Cruz Azul 2-0 on Wednesday night to win the Campeones Cup.

Messi opened the scoring in the 24th minute, heading in a cross from Luis Suárez, before turning provider for Casemiro -- sending in a corner for the Brazilian to nod home.

Sep. 12: Inter Miami 2-2 Nashville SC
In a matchup between the two best teams in the Eastern Conference, the action went end to end, with Messi getting on the scoresheet for Miami's second goal off a Rodrigo De Paul assist as he continues to lead the Golden Boot race.

Ultimately, the teams settled for a point apiece, as the hosts failed to close the gap on Nashville at the top of the table.

Sep. 9: Chicago Fire 1-1 Inter Miami

Two or Europe's greatest club players took center stage in one of the United States' most iconic American football stadiums on Wednesday -- and a record crowd came out to watch.

Ex-Bayern Munich and Barcelona star Robert Lewandowski scored a trademark acrobatic goal in the 10th minute to give the Fire an early lead at the NFL home of the Chicago Bears.

But Inter Miami drew level shortly after halftime when Casemiro, another of the game's stars with a long history of playing in Europe before moving to MLS, headed home a Messi cross from a corner kick to make it 1-1.

The assist was Messi's league-leading 13th of the season. He also has league 18 goals and is the first player in MLS history with 30-plus goal contributions in three separate seasons.

Sep. 5: Inter Miami 2-2 Atlanta United
Messi was not as effective as he was in the previous matchup, but he did get an assist for Casemiro's opening goal. However, his team was unable to win as they had to settle for a point in a 2-2 draw.

August 29: Inter Miami 7-1 CF Montréal

Fans were treated to a Messi masterclass on Saturday as the Argentine magician registered four goals and an assist to help Miami to a club-record 7-1 victory over CF Montréal.

Messi scored with a deflected free kick in the 40th minute before netting after a stunning solo run in the 52nd. After supplying an assist to Luis Suárez, the 39-year-old then completed his hat trick and with a delicate chip over the goalkeeper with seven minutes of regulation time remaining.

He wasn't done yet.

Deep into stoppage time, Messi lined up a free kick and dispatched it with trademark precision into the top corner of the net. Legendary stuff.

August 22: Inter Miami 2-1 Toronto FC

Messi's 14th MLS goal of the season wasn't enough to prevent Inter Miami from slumping to their fourth loss in their last five games, losing 2-1 to Toronto FC at Nu Stadium on Saturday.

Messi found the net with a first-time finish from a Rodrigo De Paul through-ball with eight minutes remaining, but the home side's late rally fell short of salvaging a much-needed draw to bolster the Herons' pursuit of first-placed Nashville SC in the Eastern Conference.

August 19: Inter Miami 2-2 Philadelphia Union

Messi is back scoring goals, but unfortunately, his Miami side is not back to winning ways. The Argentine scored Miami's second goal of the night as both teams finished with 10 men. Miami are now winless in their last four matches.

August 15: Nashville SC 4-1 Inter Miami
It was not the best night for Messi in Tennessee. The Argentine missed yet another penalty -- his third straight for club and country -- and they suffered a heavy 4-1 loss to their Eastern Conference rivals. However, he did get an assist for Telasco Segovia's equalizer at halftime before Miami lost control in the second half.

August 12: Inter Miami 2-3 Club León
Just days after the passing of his father, Messi came off the bench in the second half to try to help Miami continue in the Leagues Cup after they were leading 1-0. However, it ended in a 3-2 loss which saw them eliminated in the league phase after a second straight loss, coming off defeat to Monterrey last weekend with Messi away at the memorial for his father.

August 5: Inter Miami 4-2 Atlético de San Luis

Lionel Messi made his first start for Inter Miami since returning from the World Cup and picked up right where he left off, scoring a stellar pair of goals to guide his team to a come-from-behind 4-2 rout of Atlético de San Luis in its first game of the 2026 Leagues Cup.

Messi's first goal was an exquisite volley, redirecting Noah Allen's cross from the left flank while running at full speed. Miami's third goal of the opening half -- and Messi's second on the night -- came on the back of some intricate buildup play with Allen once again setting up his team captain, this time in the center of the area where he tiptoed through two defenders and buried a close-range strike past Andrés Sánchez.

The goal made Messi the all-time leading scorer in Leagues Cup history with 14, one ahead of LAFC's Denis Bouanga since the expanded competition began in 2023.

August 1: Inter Miami 2-2 Columbus Crew
Messi made his return to action for Inter Miami on Saturday, 13 days after tasting defeat with Argentina in the World Cup final. The Miami talisman started on the substitutes' bench before being introduced in the 53rd minute of the Herons' 2-2 draw with the Columbus Crew at Nu Stadium in Miami.

July 19: Spain 1-0 AET Argentina

Sunday proved to be a bridge too far for both Messi and Argentina, falling in extra time to Spain in the World Cup final.

With La Roja controlling the match basically from start to finish -- Argentina didn't register a shot on target during regulation time -- Messi had few opportunities to impact the game. Indeed, the 39-year-old was given a 3/10 in ESPN's post-match player ratings.

Still, as Mark Ogden points out, the 2026 tournament was a memorable one for Messi and cemented his status as the GOAT, if it were ever in doubt.

July 15: England 1-2 Argentina
Messi made another statement in his 205th appearance for Argentina, this time in his first-ever match against England in a World Cup semifinal. With so much at stake for both nations, Messi once again proved decisive despite not getting on the scoresheet.

He first provided the assist for Enzo Fernández's superb strike to level the match in the second half before delivering a pinpoint cross for Lautaro Martínez's headed winner, sending the reigning champions into yet another World Cup final after another dramatic encounter.

Messi has now recorded either a goal or an assist in all seven of Argentina's matches at this World Cup, and he will have the opportunity to lift the trophy for a second time when Argentina face Spain in Sunday's final in New Jersey.

July 11: Argentina 3-1 Switzerland
It was a relatively quiet night by Messi's standards as his goalscoring streak came to an end, but his influence on the match stayed the same. He set up Alexis Mac Allister's opening goal for Argentina against Switzerland, and although the match went to extra time, the defending champions won 3-1 thanks to two late goals in the second half of extra time.

Messi's quest to retain the World Cup now continues into the semifinals, where Argentina will face England for the first time in over 20 years. The clash in Atlanta -- one of international soccer's most storied rivalries -- will decide a spot in the final.

July 7: Argentina 3-2 Egypt
It was another dramatic outing for Messi and Argentina, who rallied from a 2-0 deficit to defeat Egypt 3-2 in Atlanta and book their place in the World Cup quarterfinals. As is so often the case, Messi was at the center of the action. Minutes after Egypt opened the scoring, he missed another penalty, but he quickly made amends by setting up Cristian Romero for Argentina's first goal. Messi then scored the equalizer -- his eighth goal of the tournament -- before Enzo Fernández completed the comeback with the winner. Argentina will now face Switzerland in Kansas City for a place in the semifinals.

July 3: Argentina 3-2 Cape Verde
Messi suffered a major scare in Miami Gardens on Friday evening in the round of 32, but it ultimately ended well for Argentina. He opened the scoring with his seventh goal of the tournament, extending his World Cup tally to 20 goals while finding the net in a record eighth consecutive World Cup match. Cape Verde twice fought back -- once in the second half and again in extra time -- but the world champions eventually prevailed 3-2 after extra time to book a meeting in the round of 16 with Egypt.

June 27: Jordan 1-3 Argentina
Messi didn't play the full 90 minutes in Argentina's 3-1 win over an already-eliminated Jordan, but he still made his mark during a 30-minute cameo in Texas. The 39-year-old scored a free kick for his sixth goal of the tournament and his 19th career World Cup goal, becoming the first player ever to score in seven consecutive World Cup matches. Even at 39, he's still got it.

June 22: Argentina 2-0 Austria
Another chapter in an already unparalleled career. Lionel Messi scored twice in Argentina's 2-0 win over Austria to help his team qualify for the round of 32 and become the outright leading goalscorer in men's and women's FIFA World Cup history with 18 goals. After missing an early penalty, he responded by breaking Miroslav Klose's 12-year-old record and then added a second late on to break Marta's record. All just two days before turning 39.

June 16: Argentina 3-0 Algeria
In his 200th appearance for Argentina and sixth World Cup, Lionel Messi sent a message to the world just days before his 39th birthday: he still has it. His first-ever World Cup hat trick powered Argentina to victory in their group-stage opener, while his 16th tournament goal saw him draw level with Miroslav Klose for the most goals in World Cup history.

June 9: Argentina 3-0 Iceland

Messi, working his way back from muscle fatigue ahead of the start of the World Cup, came on in the 70th minute of a pre-tournament friendly in Auburn, Alabama and scored from the penalty spot right afterward.

It was Messi's 911th career goal for club and country and 117th goal for Argentina and made him the oldest scorer in the country's soccer history.

May 24: Inter Miami 6-4 Philadelphia Union

Messi registered two assists in a scintillating performance against Philadelphia on Sunday but, unfortunately, no one was focused on results come the end of the game.

That's because, in the very last game before the World Cup, Messi left the field in the 73rd minute and headed straight to the locker room after grabbing his left thigh.

Now, supporters around the world are holding their collective breath while they wait and see if the injury has scuppered the 38-year-old's chance of appearing at a sixth World Cup.

May 13: FC Cincinnati 3-5 Inter Miami

Two goals and one assist marked yet another spectacular contribution from Miami superstar Messi on Wednesday. The Argentine magician was instrumental as the Herons fought back from 3-2 down to eventually beat Cincinnati 5-3 at TQL Stadium in Ohio.

May 9: Toronto FC 2-4 Inter Miami

It was a day of star power. Not only were Rodrigo De Paul, Luis Suárez and Sergio Reguilón all on the score sheet for the Herons, so was Messi -- and he added a pair of assists, too.

While Miami has yet to taste victory at its new home, it continues to take care of business on the road. Saturday's win in Toronto extended the club's unbeaten record away from home in 2026 to seven games, picking up six wins and one draw in the first few months of the season.

May 2: Inter Miami 3-4 Orlando City

Messi notched a goal and an assist on Saturday in what ended up being an astonishing collapse for Inter Miami at Nu Stadium.

The Herons were leading 3-0 after Messi's classy 33rd-minute strike, but gifted the visitors four goals -- including a Martín Ojeda hat trick -- to once again miss out on a victory at their new home ground. Orlando's comeback from three goals down marks only the third time in MLS history that a team has claimed all three points after trailing by three or more goals.

As for Messi's Miami, only twice has an MLS team had a longer winless run -- now up to four for the Herons -- to open up a new stadium.

April 25: Inter Miami 1-1 New England Revolution
Messi again failed to get on the scoresheet as Miami put in a fatigued second-half performance that saw them come from a goal down against New England. It was another draw -- and another game without a win at their new home, Nu Stadium.

April 22: Real Salt Lake 0-2 Inter Miami
No goals or assists from Messi as Miami visited America First Field on Wednesday, but the fans did get treated to sumptuous strikes nonetheless.

Rodrigo De Paul's opener in the 80th-minute was stunning curler from outside the box and then, almost immediately after the restart, Luis Suarez made it 2-0 with a well-struck volley.

The victory moves Inter Miami into outright second in the MLS Eastern Conference.

April 18: Colorado Rapids 2-3 Inter Miami

Another moment of Messi magic bagged all three points for Inter Miami on Saturday.

With scores level in the 79th minute, the Argentine icon danced his way past a number of Colorado defenders before curling home an outrageous effort into the far corner.

The strike -- Messi's second of the match after converting a penalty in the first half -- helped Miami to their first win under interim coach Guillermo Hoyos.

Hoyos, who had been serving as club's sporting director, took over coaching duties after Javier Mascherano unexpectedly left the club due to personal reasons last week.

April 11: Inter Miami 2-2 Red Bull New York
Miami and Messi are still waiting for a first win at Nu Stadium after a 2-2 draw with Red Bull New York on Saturday night.

Messi didn't register a goal or assist, but did help set up Germán Berterame's second-half strike that gave Inter Miami its first lead at its new home ground, but 17-year-old Adri Mehmeti's first career goal in the 77th minute secured a point for the visitors.

April 4: Inter Miami 2-2 Austin FC
Inter Miami opened Nu Stadium the only way it knows how: With a Messi goal. The No. 10 began the move in trademark style with a left-footed pass to a teammate before moving past a defender and arriving in the box at just the right time to head past goalkeeper Brad Stuver.

March 31: Argentina 5-0 Zambia
It was the last day of the month and perhaps the last game for Messi playing for Argentina playing in his native country, but they put on a show defeating the African side Zambia 5-0. Messi scored the second goal for Lionel Scaloni's side as focus will shift now to Miami until the beginning of the World Cup.

March 27: Argentina 2-1 Mauritania
In his first game for his country in 2026, Messi only played the second half as Argentina won 2-1 against Mauritania at the mythical La Bombonera in Buenos Aires, as the World Cup champions continue to prepare to defend their title this summer in North America.

March 22: NYCFC 2-3 Inter Miami

It was a thrilling encounter in the Bronx, as the Argentine star helped his team to a 3-2 win over NYCFC, which also included another trademark free kick goal, now beginning his course for potentially 1,000 career goals. Only 99 goals left!

March 18: Inter Miami 1-1 Nashville SC

Messi may have made history on Wednesday night, becoming just the second men's player in history to score 900 career goals, but it wasn't enough to seal Miami's progress in the Concacaf Champions Cup.

The Argentina legend found the back of the net in the seventh minute at Chase Stadium, but his strike was cancelled out by Nashville's Cristian Espinoza -- sealing the Herons' tournament exit on the away goals rule.

March 11: Nashville SC 0-0 Inter Miami
A drab night for Messi and Co. in the Concacaf Champions Cup. Plenty of possession but few shots on target mean that the Herons will return to Chase Stadium know a win will be needed to ensure progression.

March 7: D.C. United 1-2 Inter Miami

It was quite an eventful week for Messi. Just days before Miami's match against D.C. United, Messi and the entire squad visited the White House and met President Donald Trump and were eager to put on a show for the sold-out crowd of over 70,000 at Baltimore's M&T Bank Stadium.

And they did just that, with a 2-1 win over D.C. United. Messi, of course, scored Miami's second and is now one goal away from 900 career goals.

March 1: Orlando City 2-4 Inter Miami

Well, that blip didn't last long! Messi and Miami roared back into life with a 4-2 thrashing of Orlando on Sunday thanks to the 38-year-old's wizardry.

Things looked ominous for the Herons after the first 45 minutes, down 2-0 and looking on course to start the MLS season with two bleak losses.

But two goals and an assist from Messi in the second half dragged the visitors back in the game and helped secure Miami their first points of the season.

Feb. 21: LAFC 3-0 Inter Miami
Messi and Miami aimed to start 2026 firing on all cylinders, but it was the hosts who spoiled the defending MLS Cup champions' opener at the LA Coliseum. In front of a sellout crowd of 75,673 -- the second-highest attendance in MLS history -- Miami were outplayed, with LAFC's Denis Bouanga getting a goal and an assist in a convincing home victory.

The main talking point, however, emerged after the final whistle. Messi was initially reported to have gained unauthorized access to the officials' locker room after video circulated showing him near the area. However, it was later reported that no league policy had been violated and Messi was cleared of any wrongdoing. Miami will now turn its attention next weekend against fellow Florida side Orlando City.

stories.headline: AFL 2027 fixture: Five must-watch games in the first month
stories.summary: The 2027 AFL fixture has been released. So, to whet your appetite for the upcoming season, we've picked out the five must-watch games from the opening month.
stories.body:
The 2027 AFL fixture has been released. So, to whet your appetite for the upcoming season, we've picked out the five must-watch games from the opening month of action.

Get the popcorn ready and get set to enjoy these absolute belters in the new year.

5. Port Adelaide vs. Western Bulldogs - Round 4, Adelaide Oval, Sunday, April 8, 7:40pm (AEDT)
Make no mistake, when Zak Butters returns to Adelaide Oval to face his old mob for the first time since departing, it's going to be incredibly spicy.

In a move that shocked absolutely nobody, Butters left Port Adelaide during the 2026 trade period, inking a long-term deal with the Western Bulldogs. It's a brutal blow for the Power, and his ex-teammates will be sure to give him a hard time when they share the field in Round 4. You just know it's going to be on for young and old!

The AFL also made the move to schedule this blockbuster game as the closer to next year's Gather Round. It means far more bodies will be in Adelaide that weekend and a greater number of eyeballs on the clash.

4. Hawthorn vs. Geelong - Round 2, MCG, Monday, March 29, 3:15pm (AEDT)
The traditional Easter Monday clash between the Hawks and Cats is always on our shortlist of early season must-watch games, and next year will be no exception.

Both of these clubs are in the premiership window. Both clubs have added high-profile players this offseason. Both clubs have fanbases that bring an electric energy to Easter Monday at the MCG.

This one is also set to be a fascinating coaching battle between Chris Scott and Sam Mitchell, two of the game's best tacticians, who will go head-to-head just as much as the players on the field.

3. Fremantle vs. Western Bulldogs - Round 1, Optus Stadium, Thursday, March 18, 8:10pm (AEDT)
This Round 1 game in the west is simply oozing with intrigue.

Of course, the question on everyone's mind is how the Dockers back up after having this year's premiership ripped away from them in harrowing circumstances. Does it galvanise the club? Will we see 'Wharfie Time'? Surely not!

For the Bulldogs, they landed the biggest fish of the off-season in superstar midfielder Zak Butters. This will be the first opportunity to watch him play in his new colours, lining up in the middle alongside skipper Marcus Bontempelli and Ed Richards.

2. Brisbane vs. Collingwood - Round 2, Gabba, Thursday, March 25, 7:50pm (AEDT)
Reigning premier Brisbane will unfurl its latest flag in Round 2 when it hosts Collingwood in its first home game of the season, a clash that has blockbuster written all over it.

The Lions are looking to become just the second team ever to win four consecutive flags (joining, you guessed it, Collingwood from 1927 to 1930) but will be doing it without superstar midfielder Lachie Neale. The two-time Brownlow medallist departed for the Magpies this offseason, making this early season contest between the two clubs extra intriguing.

Plus, any opportunity to watch current Brownlow medallist Nick Daicos play footy is reason in itself to tune in!

1. Hawthorn vs. Brisbane - Round 1, MCG, Friday, March 19, 7:40pm (AEDT)
Thankfully we don't have to wait long for the Hawks and Lions -- quite possibly the competition's two best teams -- to square off in 2027. And if this game delivers even 70% of what these sides dished up in this year's epic preliminary final, then we're in for an absolute treat!

Many have labelled Brisbane's thrilling win over Hawthorn this past September as the greatest game of footy played this century. That in itself should be enough of a reason for their next clash to simply be must-watch.

There will be extra intrigue with both teams given this clash falls in Round 1. For the Lions, they will be looking to navigate life without both superstar midfielder Lachie Neale and master coach Chris Fagan, while the Hawks will be attempting to integrate recruits Zach Merrett and Ben King into their line-up.

stories.headline: Unlikely winner emerges from luckless Samoan blow
stories.summary: Ronald Volkman is set to go from Dragons discard to starting in a World Cup semi-final against Australia in the space of 12 months.
stories.body:
Chanel Harris-Tavita's luckless World Cup run looks set to play into the hands of Ronald Volkman, who looms as the obvious candidate to fill Samoa's playmaking void for their semi-final meeting with Australia.

Harris-Tavita was knocked out cold in the last World Cup final four years ago and is now long-odds to play again for Samoa this campaign.

The Warriors' No.6 strained his hamstring while taking a shot at goal in Sunday's 20-18 group stage loss to Tonga.

Parramatta half Volkman made an instant impact, scoring a try after replacing Harris-Tavita from the bench, and he will step in against the Kangaroos.

Volkman's rise to a likely Samoan starting jersey caps a terrific season for the 24-year-old after he was dumped by St George Illawarra in 2024 with concerns over a long-term shoulder issue.

Samoa face Australia on Sunday at Sydney's Allianz Stadium after their narrow loss to the Tongans dumped England out of the tournament on points differential.

"Ronald's done a great job, he did a fantastic job last week for us in the win over Papua New Guinea," Samoa coach Ben Gardiner said.

"He came on at the back end of the game, in a slightly different role for a different reason and he did a really good job when he came on.

"I thought he brought great energy, I thought his speed in the line really put pressure on the Tongan team.

"We've got trust in every player in our team, so it doesn't matter who goes on.

"The guys that are in our squad, we've got complete trust in them."

The 24-year-old Volkman is likely to be the target of heavy traffic from the Kangaroos' edge forwards as the two sides renew a rivalry that has simmered since the World Cup final four years ago.

Samoa have yet to beat Australia in a Test across fives meetings and lost 38-12 in their last international three years ago.

"Their form's been very strong, very strong and they've got fantastic players," Gardiner said.

"They've got players that have played a lot of games for the Kangaroos and are in a really good position at the moment.

"They've won three footy matches on the trot, and they're going to be a really hard side to beat next week.

"If we hold on to the ball and we complete better than 66 per cent that'll give us a good opportunity to pick up on some of those things we need to work on."
